title: Lauren Steadman: How Paralympic gold led to Celebrity MasterChef glory, career, net worth and personal life in focus
text: Lauren Steadman: How Paralympic gold led to Celebrity MasterChef glory, career, net worth and personal life in focus Lauren Steadman has added another major title to a career already filled with Paralympic medals. The British athlete won Celebrity MasterChef 2026 after beating Olympic weightlifter Emily Campbell and Love Island star Shakira Khan in the BBC One final. Steadman impressed judges Grace Dent and Giorgio Locatelli with a three-course menu, with her sticky toffee pudding playing an important part in the decision. The victory gives the 33-year-old another television success after Strictly Come Dancing and Celebrity SAS: Who Dares Wins. But away from TV, Steadmanâs biggest achievements have come in swimming and paratriathlon. How did Lauren Steadman win Celebrity MasterChef 2026 with Emily Campbell and Shakira Khan Steadman won the Celebrity MasterChef 2026 final on September 18 after the three finalists were asked to cook a three-course meal for Dent and Locatelli. The series started with 15 celebrities before the competition was reduced to the final three. Her menu began with pan-fried scallops in chilli butter, served with coconut and spinach lentil dahl puree and fresh apple batons. For the main course, she prepared beef Wellington with truffle mash, caramelised shallots, butternut squash puree, tenderstem broccoli and red wine jus. The dessert was a classic sticky toffee pudding with dates, caramel sauce and clotted cream ice cream. It proved to be a key moment in the final. Locatelli praised the pudding, while Dent also spoke highly of Steadmanâs food. Steadman was visibly emotional after hearing the result. She said: âThis is up there with a Paralympic gold medal. There havenât been many moments when I have been left speechless but this is one of them.â The final followed several demanding challenges during the series. Steadman had already cooked for guests at Crufts and taken part in the Chefâs Table at The Ritz. Steadmanâs final menu helped her secure the trophy, while also noting her earlier Paralympic success. What are Lauren Steadmanâs Paralympic achievements and sports records Before becoming a television regular, Steadman built her name in elite sport. Born in Peterborough, she started swimming at a young age and represented Great Britain at the Beijing 2008 Paralympic Games when she was 15. She returned to the pool at London 2012. Her results did not bring a Paralympic medal, but the experience helped shape what came next. Steadman later moved into paratriathlon after her uncle, who is also a triathlete, encouraged her to try the sport. Her first British triathlon came in 2011, when she finished second. Her first Paralympic triathlon medal came at Rio 2016, where she won silver in the sportâs Paralympic debut. Five years later, she went one step further at Tokyo 2020, winning gold in the womenâs PTS5 event. At Paris 2024, Steadman returned to the podium with bronze in the same classification. That gave her a full set of Paralympic triathlon medals: silver, gold and bronze. According to ParalympicsGB, Steadman is a three-time World Champion and has won eight European titles. She was also appointed MBE in the 2022 New Year Honours for services to triathlon. What TV shows has Lauren Steadman appeared on after her Paralympic career Steadmanâs television career began long before Celebrity MasterChef. In 2018, she joined Strictly Come Dancing with professional dancer AJ Pritchard. She reached the semi-finals and became the first female contestant with a disability to take part in the BBC show. Her next major television challenge came with Celebrity SAS: Who Dares Wins. Steadman reached the final stage of the competition and was later crowned a joint winner of the series. She also appeared on Richard Osmanâs House of Games before taking on Celebrity MasterChef in 2026. The television appearances have given audiences a different look at Steadman outside competition. Strictly tested her dancing, SAS put her through demanding physical and mental challenges, while MasterChef moved her into a completely different setting. Her professional work also includes motivational speaking and business activity. Steadmanâs official website describes her work around mindset, performance and helping people deal with perceived barriers. She is also linked to Sizu, a motivational wellness clothing brand. What is Lauren Steadmanâs net worth, education and personal life According to LatestCelebArticles, Lauren Steadmanâs net worth is estimated at between $1 million and $5 million. However, the website does not provide financial records or details showing how the figure was calculated, so the estimate cannot be independently confirmed. Her income is linked to her sporting career, television appearances, sponsorships and other professional work. The University of Portsmouthâs profile of the Paralympic champion confirms that, alongside her sporting and television career, she has also been involved in entrepreneurial work. Her income has come from several areas over the years, including elite sport, television work, sponsorships, speaking engagements and business projects. Her exact earnings from Celebrity MasterChef and her other television appearances have not been publicly disclosed. Steadman also has a strong academic background. She studied Psychology at the University of Portsmouth, graduating with a first-class degree in 2014. She later completed an MSc in Business and Management with distinction in 2017. The University of Portsmouth has highlighted both degrees in its profiles of Steadman. The university also notes her sporting achievements, including her Rio silver, Tokyo gold and Paris bronze. She has spoken publicly about the role her family played in her early sporting journey, while her uncle was the person who encouraged her to try triathlon after her swimming career. She went from a teenage Paralympic swimmer to a world-class paratriathlete, won gold at Tokyo 2020, returned for bronze in Paris, appeared on major British television shows and has now added the Celebrity MasterChef trophy to her record. title: American star Gabby Thomas apologizes on X after fan backlash for failing to recognize Usain Boltâs baby photo in Olympics quiz
text: Gabby Thomas (Image Via Getty) American sprint star Gabby Thomas has apologized after a viral Olympics social media video showed her failing to recognize a childhood photo of Usain Bolt. The Paris 2024 triple Olympic gold medalist laughed after struggling to identify the Jamaican sprint legend, leading to criticism from fans online. Thomas later addressed the backlash on X. She admitted that she was embarrassed by the moment and apologized for both not recognizing Bolt and laughing during the quiz. She also explained that she grew up watching Bolt and other Black track athletes who inspired her generation. Gabby Thomas opens up on Usain Boltâs baby photo mistake The incident happened during a promotional trivia segment shared by the Olympicsâ social media channels. Athletes were shown childhood photographs of famous track and field stars and asked to identify them. When Gabby Thomas was shown a baby picture of Usain Bolt, she could not recognize him. Her reaction included laughter, which quickly became a talking point among fans on social media. Some viewers criticized Thomas for failing to identify one of the biggest names in athletics history. Bolt is widely regarded as one of the greatest sprinters ever. He holds the world records in both the 100m and 200m and won multiple Olympic gold medals during his legendary career. As the clip continued to circulate, Thomas decided to respond to the criticism. She took to X and directly addressed the reaction to the video. âI want to genuinely apologize to everyone I upset for not recognizing Usain Bolt in his baby photo the other day on the Olympics social media video. I shouldnât have laughed about it either. I am so embarrassed. I promise to unpack this and will do betterâ, she wrote. Thomas then offered more context about her connection to Bolt and the influence he had on her generation of athletes. âI grew up watching Usain Bolt among many other Black track athletes. They inspired me and showed my generation of athletes what Black excellence looks like (on and off the track). I know what he and Noah look like- their baby photos just stumped me. But they shouldnât have. I would choose to be black in every lifetimeâ, she continued in her second tweet. Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines She also explained why she decided to respond publicly after initially choosing not to address the controversy. âI normally wouldnât respond, but my comments and DMs are being flooded on every social platform. I fear I really upset my communityâ, she concluded in her third tweet. The controversy came as Thomas and Bolt were both connected to the inaugural World Athletics Ultimate Championship in Budapest. Bolt attended the event as a headline ambassador and was seen taking part in promotional activities around the $10 million competition. Thomas also competed at the championship. She finished second in the womenâs 200m final in 21.77 seconds, behind fellow American Melissa Jefferson-Wooden. Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

title: Pak to play Asian Champions Trophy in Punjab, face India on Nov 1: CM Mann
text: Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann with Hockey Indiaâs secretary general Bhola Nath Singh, director general Cdr RK Srivastava, executive board member RP Singh and Hockey Punjab president Nitin Kohli in Mohali on Monday Mohali : Punjab will host the Menâs Asian Champions Trophy for the first time from Oct 27 to Nov 5, featuring a high-stakes clash between India and Pakistan in Jalandhar on Nov 1, chief minister Bhagwant Mann announced on Monday. Mann, who unveiled the tournament logo in Mohali alongside Hockey India officials, said the Centre permits Pakistan to compete in multi-lateral sporting events on Indian soil, even though bilateral series remain suspended The six-nation tournament features India, Pakistan, Japan, South Korea, Malaysia and China, with Oman and Bangladesh named as reserve teams. All league-stage matches will be played at Jalandharâs Olympian Surjit Singh Hockey Stadium. The action will then move to Mohaliâs Olympian Balbir Singh (Senior) International Hockey Stadium for the semi-finals on Nov 4 and the final on Nov 5. Mann said the participation of Pakistan adds immense sporting weight to the championship. âThe India-Pakistan clash at 7 pm on Nov 1 in Jalandhar will be one of the biggest attractions of the tournament,â Mann said. âAn India-Pakistan match is not about hatredâit is about the passion for hockey, the roar of the spectators, and the beauty of the sport,â he said. Hockey India secretary general Bhola Nath Singh highlighted the strong relationship between the two hockey federations. âIf the Indian team defeats Pakistan, I make it a point to meet their team first,â he shared. To support the event, CM Mann announced an allocation of Rs 25.40 crore, including Rs 22.96 crore for upgrading the venues in Jalandhar (Rs 14 crore) and Mohali (Rs 8.96 crore). He also announced free entry for all spectators to boost crowd engagement Calling the event an âemotional homecomingâ for a sport deeply rooted in Punjabâs history, Mann highlighted the stateâs rich athletic legacy. Punjab has produced more than 50 Olympic medallists and 10 national captains, including legends like Olympian Balbir Singh Sr, Udham Singh and Ajit Pal Singh, who have inspired generations, he said. âEven today, this tradition continues. During the Paris 2024 Olympics, Punjab had 10 players representing India, with Harmanpreet Singh leading the national side,â Mann added. Defending champions India enter the tournament aiming to retain their title, having previously won back-to-back championships in Chennai (2023) and Hulunbuir, China (2024). PUNJAB TO BID FOR 2030 HOCKEY WORLD CUP MATCHES: MANN Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann said India will host the Hockey World Cup in 2030 and Punjab will stake its claim to host matches of that prestigious tournament as well. âSuccessful organisation of the Asian Champions Trophy will strengthen that case. Our govt is preparing not just two stadiums, but a message for the sporting world. We have the infrastructure, the talent and sporting culture to host the big international events,â he said. title: Paralympic star Lauren Steadman seals Celebrity MasterChef crown after nail-biting finale
text: Lauren Steadman. Image via: BBC Lauren Steadman has won Celebrity MasterChef, and the Paralympic champion needed every single course to do it. Three finalists cooked a three-course meal for judges Grace Dent and Giorgio Locatelli on Friday night, and only one could lift the 2026 trophy. The BBC One final capped a contest that began with 15 celebrities. Olympic medallist Emily Campbell and Love Island's Shakira Khan pushed hard, and Dent found the choice close to impossible. One dessert tipped the verdict, though, and a runner-up had a joke ready afterwards. Lauren Steadman beats Celebrity MasterChef rivals in dramatic final showdown Lauren Steadman took the title on Friday, September 18, in a final shown on BBC One and iPlayer at 8 p.m. The Paralympic gold medallist beat Campbell and Khan in a head-to-head where each finalist had to cook and present a faultless three-course meal. It was the last chance to show passion and creativity in front of Dent and Locatelli, and Steadman's execution earned her the trophy. Steadman opened with scallops pan-fried in chilli butter, served with a coconut and spinach lentil dahl puree and topped with fresh apple batons. The main was a beef wellington with truffle mash, caramelised shallot, butternut squash puree, tenderstem broccoli and a red wine jus. Dessert was a classic sticky toffee pudding with dates, caramel sauce and clotted cream ice cream. The pudding did the most damage. Locatelli said, "Mamma mia... this is the best sticky toffee pudding I've ever had." Dent went with "exemplary" for the same dish and said the final plates were simply wonderful. Locatelli also explained the bigger picture. Steadman has a knack for turning every situation into an advantage, and that is why the crown went to the champion. Finals week added plenty of pressure. Steadman made a dog bone shaped dessert for fifty guests at Crufts, billed as the world's largest and most prestigious dog show. The Chef's Table at The Ritz, a top event on the culinary calendar, was another test. After the win, Steadman said, "This is up there with a Paralympic gold medal." Speechless moments are rare, Steadman added, and this was one of them. Lauren Steadman's Celebrity MasterChef win adds to a long sporting rÃ©sumÃ© Steadman is an MBE, was born in Peterborough and is a University of Portsmouth graduate. Swimming came first, at the 2008 Beijing Paralympics at age 15 and again at London 2012. Paratriathlon followed, bringing silver in Rio 2016, gold in Tokyo and bronze in Paris 2024. The three-time world champion is also an eight-time European champion. Steadman reached the Strictly Come Dancing semi-finals in 2018 as the show's first female contestant with a disability, then finished as a finalist on Celebrity SAS: Who Dares Wins in 2019. title: Inspiring story of the day: "My middle school said I should be playing with dolls": How Sabrina Ionescu turned rejection into an NCAA record and WNBA championship
text: How Sabrina Ionescu turned rejection into an NCAA record and WNBA championship(Getty Images) Some inspiring sports stories begin with championships and records, while others begin with a young athlete being told there is no place for her. For Sabrina Ionescu, one of those moments came in middle school when she wanted to play basketball but her school did not have enough girls to form a team. Instead of walking away from the sport, Ionescu found another way to keep playing. Years later, she became an NCAA record-holder, the No. 1 overall pick in the WNBA Draft, an Olympic gold medalist and a champion with the New York Liberty. How Sabrina Ionescu responded when her middle school told her to play with dolls Basketball was already a major part of Sabrina Ionescu's childhood. She grew up playing with boys and also competed on a club team. Her twin brother Eddy played basketball too, and Ionescu sometimes filled in for his all-male team when they needed another player. Her middle school presented a different problem. There were not enough girls to form a team, and when Ionescu wanted to play with the boys, the school did not allow her to join them. Years later, she remembered exactly what she was told. âMy middle school said I should be playing with dolls. Seriously, word-for-word,âIonescu said in a 2019 interview with The Washington Post. The comment could have pushed a young athlete away from the sport. Ionescu responded differently. She started looking for girls who could join the team so there would be enough players for a girls' basketball team. âSo I went out and recruited a bunch of girls to sign up for the team, and then I would just play,â she said. The story was not simply about getting onto a school team. It also showed how Ionescu learned to create opportunities when they were not immediately available. Playing against boys also forced her to find different ways to contribute. She recalled situations where the boys did not want to pass the ball to her, so she focused on rebounding and creating her own chances. When she played with older athletes, she could use passing to influence the game even when she was physically smaller. Those skills later became central to her identity as a player. Sabrina Ionescu was not simply a scorer. She could rebound, pass and create plays for teammates, which eventually made her one of the most complete guards in college basketball. The girl who had once been told there was no place for her on the boys' team was already learning how to make herself useful on the court without waiting for someone else to give her an opportunity. How Sabrina Ionescu turned those early setbacks into an NCAA record Sabrina Ionescu's move to the University of Oregon took her basketball career to another level. She quickly became one of the biggest stars in college basketball and built a record that still defines her legacy. She finished her Oregon career with 26 triple-doubles, an NCAA record across men's and women's basketball. She also became the only NCAA player to reach 2,000 points, 1,000 assists and 1,000 rebounds. Her final college numbers showed just how unusual her all-around game was. Ionescu recorded 2,562 points, 1,040 rebounds and 1,091 assists during her Oregon career. The numbers were especially notable because they reflected the same skills she had developed when she was younger. Rebounding had once been a way to stay involved when teammates did not pass to her. Passing later became one of the strongest parts of her game. At Oregon, those skills helped her become a player capable of controlling a game in several ways. Her rise also brought her into the orbit of some of basketball's biggest names. Kobe Bryant became an important influence during her development, and Ionescu later spoke about how much she learned from watching his approach to the game. âHe had such attention to detail, just all the small fundamental things,â Ionescu said in an interview with Vanity Fair. Bryant's death in January 2020 came shortly before Ionescu entered the WNBA. She had looked up to him for years and later explained how much his example influenced her. That same year, another major chapter began. The New York Liberty selected Ionescu with the No. 1 overall pick in the 2020 WNBA Draft. The selection placed huge expectations on a player who had already become one of the most decorated athletes in college basketball. Her first professional season, however, did not go according to plan. Ionescu injured her left ankle in her third WNBA game and missed the rest of the 2020 season. Instead of getting a full rookie campaign, she had to spend much of the year recovering and preparing for another chance. She eventually returned to the court and continued developing into one of the Liberty's leading players. The following years brought more milestones. Ionescu earned her place among the league's top players and represented the United States at the 2024 Paris Olympics, where she won a gold medal. But another major opportunity was waiting in New York. How Sabrina Ionescu helped the New York Liberty win their first WNBA championship The Liberty reached the 2024 WNBA Finals and faced the Minnesota Lynx in a series that went all the way to Game 5.The deciding game took place at Barclays Center, giving New York a chance to win the first championship in franchise history in front of its home crowd. The game went to overtime before the Liberty won 67-62. Ionescu's individual numbers in the deciding game were unusual for her. She shot 1-for-19 from the field and 1-for-10 from three-point range, finishing with five points. Yet she still contributed seven rebounds and eight assists while playing 39 minutes and 39 seconds. The Liberty did not need Ionescu to have her best shooting night to finish the job. New York found contributions from across the roster and secured the championship that had eluded the franchise since its first WNBA season in 1997. For Sabrina Ionescu, the championship added another major achievement to a career that had already included an NCAA record, the No. 1 overall draft selection and Olympic gold. Her story also extends beyond what happened on the court. Ionescu has spoken about wanting to give young athletes opportunities that she did not always have growing up. Through her SI20 Foundation, she has worked on initiatives connected to youth sports and education. In her Vanity Fair interview, she explained why she wanted to start that work early rather than wait until later in life. "I didn't want to wait to do it when I was 35; I wanted to start this while I was young,â she said. That idea connects with the story of her childhood. When her middle school did not give her an obvious route onto the court, she recruited girls and created another route herself. Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines Years later, she had the platform to help create opportunities for other young athletes. She did not respond by leaving basketball behind. She kept playing, developed an all-around game, broke NCAA records, became the No. 1 overall WNBA pick, won Olympic gold and helped the New York Liberty win their first championship. Her journey was not built around one dramatic moment. It came through years of playing against older athletes, finding ways to contribute, recovering from setbacks and continuing to improve. The young Sabrina Ionescu who had to recruit girls just to form a school team eventually became one of the defining players of her generation. And the response to being told to play with dolls was simple: she kept playing basketball. Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

title: Celine Dion returns to Paris residency after two years: âI made a promise to come backâ¦ So here I am!â
text: Celine Dion returns to the stage after two years for her Paris residency. (Instagram) Celine Dion has officially returned to the stage after two years! The singer recently sang for the first time in almost two years during the first show of her Paris residency. The singer last performed during the Olympic Opening Ceremony on July 26, 2024, when she sang âHymne Ã  l'amourâ from the Eiffel Tower. While returning to the stage to perform full sets of her songs in Paris, Dion was left in an emotional state as she addressed fans. Celine Dion gets emotional during her first performance in two years On Saturday, September 12, the iconic singer took the stage for the first time in two years to perform a full show. She performed at PlÃ©nitude Arena (formerly the Paris La DÃ©fense Arena) in Nanterre, France, for the opening night of her 26-show residency with her 1998 song âOn Ne Change Pas.â However, moments into the song, Dion had to completely stop herself from singing as she got choked up over the overwhelming opportunity. PEOPLE reported that Dion was seen wiping away tears at the time before resuming the song with full zeal. She then performed another track titled 'Destiny' before finally addressing the crowd who were there in her support. She shared in French and English, âThere are many of you here tonight from all over the world. Thank you so very much for coming. If itâs your first time in Paris. I hope you fall in love with it, just like I did. Finally, itâs amazing we are all together. I made a promise. I made a promise to come back, to be back on stage. So here I am, singing for you and singing for me, singing life!â She concluded, âThank you so very much for your support and your patience, and if I may say so: I am everything I am because you loved me. â This was also the singerâs first full concert since she last performed a full set in 2020 during her âCourage Tour.' However, at the time, because of the COVID-19 pandemic and her stiff person syndrome diagnosis, Dion had to cancel the remainder of her tour and had to take a break from her career altogether to rest and recover. About Celine Dionâs stiff person syndrome diagnosis In 2022, the âMy Heart Will Go Onâ star revealed to the world that she had been diagnosed with stiff person syndrome and had to take a break from her career. According to a Harperâs BAZAAR report published in August this year, the singer had been facing symptoms of the disease for the past 17 years, and she only received an official diagnosis much later in life. Talking about the syndrome to the outlet, Dion shared, âIt is a progressive condition. I donât like to say âdisease.â Disease makes you go like this: âKevin, youâre such a disease.ââ Cleveland Clinic states, âStiff person syndrome (SPS) is a rare autoimmune neurological disorder that causes muscle stiffness in your trunk and abdomen (the middle part of your body). Over time, you may also develop stiffness (rigidity) and spasms in your legs and other muscles. Walking may be difficult, and you may become more prone to falls and injury.â The singer will appear for 25 more shows for her Paris residency, which was increased after millions of fans tried to book tickets for her show. She will perform a couple of shows in September and October and will resume in March 2027 to complete the remainder of her residency. Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. title: Simone Biles built a custom $3 million waterfront mansion in Texas; after years of planning and delays, the Olympian settled into the lakefront estate following a prior $1.1 million property buy
text: Simone Biles built a custom $3 million waterfront mansion in Texas; after years of planning and delays, the Olympian settled into the lakefront estate following a prior $1.1 million property buy Simone Biles and her husband Jonathan Owens have finally moved into the Texas home they spent years planning and building. The custom lakefront mansion near Houston was completed on November 11, 2025, after the couple began working on its design in 2020. The project took much longer than they first expected, with Biles sharing updates as the house slowly took shape. The seven-time Olympic medalist and Owens chose to build the home from the ground up instead of buying a finished property. The result is a large lakefront house with spaces designed around their everyday life, pets and love of sports. When did Simone Biles and Jonathan Owens start building their Texas mansion The story of Simone Biles and Jonathan Owensâ new home began in 2020, when they started planning the property. Biles later explained that simply getting the design ready took about a year. The next wait came from the homeowners association. According to Biles, the required approvals took time, which pushed the actual start of construction to February 2022. That meant the couple had already spent a long time thinking about the house before construction even began. Once work started, Biles continued to share photos and videos showing the property at different stages, from the early framework to the finished rooms. The house was expected to take far less time. After years of waiting, Biles summed up her frustration in a short Instagram update: "They lied when they said nine months to build!" She also shared the timeline behind the project, writing: "Home building requires a lot of patience." Biles later explained: "Started the design process in 2020 and took a year to complete," before adding, "Approvals took a while from [the] HOA; broke ground in Feb 2022; completed 11/11/25." The project therefore stretched across several major moments in the couple's lives. They got married in 2023, while Biles also returned to competition and competed at the Paris Olympics in 2024. What is inside Simone Biles and Jonathan Owensâ $3 million lakefront home The home was built around a mix of comfort, entertainment and spaces that fit the couple's interests. The property has been widely estimated at around $3 million, although the exact final cost has not been publicly confirmed. One of the main features is the kitchen. It has two large islands, custom cabinets and black-and-white marble details. Large glass doors also connect the living areas with the outdoor space and lake views. The house also has a primary bathroom with a large marble finish, two sinks and a spacious shower. There is a game room, home theater and wet bar, giving the couple several areas to spend time at home. Sports are also part of the property. The outdoor area includes a swimming pool and spa beside the lake, along with a basketball court. An in-ground trampoline has also been built close to the water. The house has several personal touches that make it different from a standard luxury property. Biles and Owens have a separate room for their dogs, complete with a pet spa area and built-in feeding space. The room uses the same black-and-white look seen in other parts of the house. The laundry room is another detail Biles has highlighted. Instead of sharing one set of machines, the couple have separate washers and dryers. Biles joked about the reason behind that decision, writing: "Since Jonathan always wants to do laundry the exact same day as me," and then adding, "Now [there is] one set for each of us." How did Simone Bilesâ earlier $1.1 million Texas property compare with the new mansion Before the lakefront house was completed, Biles already had a Texas home where she and Owens spent time during the construction period. Realtor.com reported in 2024 that Biles bought the contemporary Spring, Texas, property in 2020. The 4,000-square-foot home has four bedrooms and 3.5 bathrooms and sits on just over an acre. The property had been listed for $863,500 in 2020, but the exact amount Biles paid was not publicly confirmed. That makes the often-repeated $1.1 million purchase figure difficult to verify. The earlier home also had several features that suited Biles' lifestyle, including a large kitchen, open living areas, a primary suite and a mud room with a pet-washing and feeding area. It also appeared in the Netflix documentary series âSimone Biles Rising,â which followed the gymnast's life and return to elite competition. The new lakefront property is a different kind of home. Rather than taking an existing house and adapting it, Biles and Owens had the chance to decide what they wanted from the beginning. That included the layout, sports areas, pet space and entertainment rooms. When did Simone Biles and Jonathan Owens finally move into the new Texas home The house was officially completed in November 2025, but the couple did not immediately settle into it full time. At the time, Jonathan Owens was playing for the Chicago Bears, meaning the couple spent part of their time in Chicago. After the NFL season ended, Biles began sharing more pictures from the Texas property as the couple started making the house their home. Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines In February 2026, Biles showed more of the finished interiors, including her closet and office area. The couple had also returned to Texas after their time in Chicago. Architectural Digest reported that Simone Biles had followed the project closely for about almost five years, documenting the transformation from an unfinished structure into the completed lakefront home. The long wait finally gave the athlete couple a house built around their own needs rather than a property they had simply purchased and moved into. Biles' latest home also comes at a different stage of her life. She has already competed in three Olympic Games and remains one of the most decorated gymnasts in history. Jonathan Owens' NFL career has also taken the couple to different cities. For now, their custom Texas house gives them a home base that was designed by them from the start. In 2026, Biles also said she planned to spend time in Indianapolis to support Owens after he joined the Colts, so the Texas property is not necessarily where the couple will spend every month of the year. Still, after five years of planning, waiting and construction, the lakefront home has finally become part of their lives. Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

title: After Olympic glory, Manu Bhaker chases the one medal missing from her collection at Asian Games
text: Manu Bhaker PUNE: There is something about Manu Bhaker . Other than being a double Olympic medallist, a former world No. 1, World Championships medallist, there is that something extra that makes Manu what she is today â a fierce competitor even when she is not the best-ranked shooter on the team. Although, the 24-year-old has come a long way and has a little left to prove to her doubters, there is something that Manu would like to tick for herself â an individual medal at the Asian Games . Watch Ancy Sojan targets Asian Games gold after historic 6.88m leap In her participation at the last two editions, 2018 and 2023, Manu finished fifth and sixth. While she had participated in two events at Jakarta 2018, Manu shot only in the 25m pistol at Hangzhou. The Haryana girl is back to shooting in two events at Aichi-Nagoya. The way she has been shooting over the years, it is difficult to say which is her favourite, the 25m pistol or the 10m air pistol. Maybe it is an evolution of sorts. Her Serbian coach, Jelena Arunovic, feels Manuâs presence in the field is not just defined by her achievements. âI think an athlete is defined not just by achievements, but also by longevity. If someone has been competing at the highest level for almost 10 years, regularly reaching finals and standing on international podiums, I donât think there is a better rÃ©sume than that,â the Olympic gold-winning coach told TOI. After six months of her stay in India and spending hours at the range with the shooter, Jelena, you could say, has deep insight on what the unique Manu psyche is. The Indian shooter has gone through some difficult times, personally. After her coach Jaspal Rana passed away suddenly in June, she lost her grandmother last week. Arunovic however feels Manu is a fighter and nothing stops her from working hard. âTechnically, she has a very strong foundation and a huge amount of experience. Mentally and temperamentwise, she is a fighter. She wants to improve, she asks questions, she thinks about what she is doing, and she is willing to work even when something is difficult or uncomfortable,â the coach said. Arunovic feels that not just in India, Manu and other Indian shooters enjoy a lot of respect abroad as well. âThere is a common belief in shooting that Chinese and Indian athletes train more than anyone else. I have now worked in both countries, and I can say that, in my experience, Indians work more than the Chinese. Manu is definitely part of that culture of hard work,â the coach said. âManu is respected not only because of her results, but also because of the level she has maintained for many years. I think people in India may sometimes underestimate how much respect Indian shooters have abroad. At international competitions, everyone knows who they are and what they are capable of.â Arunovic, who had guided her sister Zorana to the Paris 2024 gold, feels Manu doesnât lack motivation and her quest to constantly keep her on top makes her different. âFor me, this is the difference between external and internal motivation. External motivation depends on applause, recognition, support, or rewards. Internal motivation does not. When external motivation disappears, everything can stop but an athlete who genuinely wants to be the best does not adjust according to whether people applaud, support or doubt them. Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines âAthletes with strong internal motivation are usually their own biggest critics. They constantly look for what can be better, what can be improved, and what more can be done. Manu is a very good example of that, but I see the same quality across the Indian team,â she explained. Other than the two individual events, Manu will also vie for the team medals with Suruchi Phogat and Esha Singh in the 10m air pistol event and Rahi Sarnobat and Esha in the 25m pistol events. title: Meet Yaylagul Ramazanova: The archer, pregnant at 6.5 months who shot a perfect 10 after feeling her baby kick at the Paris Olympics; now her baby also shares love for the sport
text: Photo: @yaylagulramazanova/ Instagram The Olympics often bring us some dramatic breakthroughs that leave behind a trail of inspirational stories, but only a few as unusual as this one. At the Paris 2024 Games, Azerbaijani archer Yaylagul Ramazanova stepped onto the field six and a half months pregnant, competing against rivals half her age and twice her experience. What happened next turned her into an unlikely fan favorite. Down to the wire in a tiebreaker against a heavily experienced Chinese opponent, Ramazanova felt something unexpected, and what happened next was anything but ordinary. Her story is no less miraculous, almost like a blessing from above. Letâs dig in to find out who she is and what her story is about. Who is Yaylagul Ramazanova Yaylagul Ramazanova is an archer from Azerbaijan who made headlines at the Paris 2024 Olympics. At 34, she competed at the games while being six and a half months pregnant, becoming only the second archer from her country ever to reach the platform. Ramazanova actually started out as a shooter before switching to archery, after a coach noticed her long arms might suit the sport better. Her story at the games became an example of motherhood and the bond a mother and baby share with each other even before the child is born in the world. Ramazanovaâs baby kicked, and she hit a perfect score Ramazanova, 34, was competing in her first Olympics, but her toughest test came early, in the women's individual elimination round against China's An Qixuan, an archer who had entered the match as the favourite. The two were locked at 5-5, forcing a tiebreaker where each competitor gets just one arrow to decide the outcome. That's when Ramazanova says her baby stepped in. "I felt my baby kick me before I shot this last arrow, and then I shot a 10," Ramazanova told Chinese state news agency Xinhua News. While An Qixuan scored a 9, Ramazanova's perfect shot sent her through to the round of 16 of the games. She trained throughout her pregnancy Ramazanova, who initially competed in shooting before switching to archery, said she never saw her pregnancy as something working against her during preparation for the Games. Instead, she described it as a source of strength. "I didn't feel uncomfortable with my pregnancy," Ramazanova said to Xinhua News. "Instead, I felt that I was not fighting alone, but fighting together with my baby." ID@undefined Caption not available. ID@undefined Caption not available. ID@undefined Caption not available. ID@undefined Caption not available. That mindset carried her through months of demanding training, all while visibly pregnant in front of the world. Ramazanova was ultimately eliminated in the round of 16, losing to Germany's Michelle Kroppen. Still, by that point, her run had already made her one of the most famous and inspirational stories of the Paris Games. Her baby also now loves the sport The Olympicsâ official handle reveals that a few months later her daughter Alifa was born and she âlikes to shoot and Iâm thinking she will maybe do archery, I hope so!â She drew support from fellow competitors She also earned admiration from fellow competitors, including American archer Casey Kaufhold, who at the time was ranked world No. 1, said to the Associated Press, "I think it's awesome that we see more expecting mothers shooting in the Olympic Games and it's great to have one in the sport of archery". She further added, "I think it's awesome for this archer that one day, she can tell her kid, 'Hey, I went to the Olympic Games, and you were there, too'". She added that Ramazanova's coach was also a mother, and that seeing that kind of support system made the moment feel even more meaningful. Looking for trusted parenting advice? text: People cross the flooded streets following a heavy rain in Nagoya, central Japan Tuesday, Sept. 8, 2026. title: Who is Tennis star Andy Murrayâs wife Kim Sears? Her art career, family life, business interests and role at Cromlix House in 2026
text: Andy Murray and Kim Sears' combined net worth: Inside their journey from Grand Slam wins to business growth and family focus (Image Via Getty Images) Andy Murray âs wife Kim Sears has lived a lot of her life with one of Britainâs most successful tennis players, but sheâs also made a name for herself away from the game. Sears grew up in a tennis family and has made a living painting portraits and animals, and has generally steered clear of the intense celebrity spotlight surrounding her husband. In 2026, Sears is best known for her ownership of Cromlix, the luxury Scottish country house hotel she co-owns with Murray. The couple purchased the property in 2013 and took over management, with Sears playing a major creative and strategic role in its evolution. Watch Andy Murray marries girlfriend Kim Sears in Dunblane Who is Andy Murrayâs wife Kim Sears? Kim Sears was born December 10, 1987, in Sussex, England. She grew up around professional tennis with her father, Nigel Sears being a former pro and highly respected coach. The pair first met at the US Open in 2005, and their connection began. As Murray started to rise the professional tennis ladder, the relationship blossomed. Sears became a regular sight on the major tournament circuit, helping Murray through the biggest moments of his career. The pair married in Dunblane, Scotland, on April 11, 2015. Their family has since grown to four kids. Murray is a global star, but the couple have largely kept their children away from too much exposure. Away from tennis, Sears has also been an avid artist, especially in the fields of portraits and animal paintings. She has also taken a creative interest in her approach to Cromlix, with which she has been closely involved in terms of interiors, artwork, furnishings and ambience throughout the property. Sears is the creative force behind the hotel venture, Cromlix says, and has been involved in details from upholstery and florals to artwork and menu design. Kim Sears and Andy Murrayâs family life Andy Murray's professional tennis career will officially end after he competes at the 2024 Paris Olympics. His retirement marked a big change for the family after nearly two decades dominated by travelling the world, tournaments and training. Murray, who retired from tennis earlier this year, said he has enjoyed having more time with his children and wife in retirement. The former world No. 1 has also taken up golf and other interests and remained active in business interests. Family detail Information Wife Kim Sears Marriage April 11, 2015 Children Four Current family base Surrey, England Andy Murray retirement 2024 Paris Olympics Since then, the couple's life off the court has been more about family and business than the rigours of the ATP Tour. In a 2026 interview, Murray said he was enjoying the day-to-day routine of family life after years of travelling the globe. Kim Sears and Andy Murrayâs Cromlix journey Cromlix has become one of the most significant projects to be associated with Kim Sears and Andy Murray. The couple bought the Victorian country estate near Dunblane in 2013, in part because of its strong links to the Murray family and the local community. The property re-opened as a luxury hotel in 2014. Its significance is especially personal in that Murrayâs grandparents marked their silver wedding anniversary at Cromlix and the couple later celebrated their wedding there. The Murrays took over the hotelâs management themselves in 2023 after a period of working with an external management company. Sears then became deeply involved in the direction of the property, including design, staffing, budgeting and the overall guest experience. The hotelâs current aesthetic eschews a traditional, tartan-heavy Scottish country-house style. Indeed, botanical themes, Scottish artwork, local suppliers and contemporary interiors have been woven throughout the estate. Set in 34 acres of woodland and landscaped grounds, Cromlix has a chapel and lochan. In the hotel's official description, the couple talk of their vision to provide a relaxed contemporary country-house experience. title: Meet Cameron Myers, the 20-year-old Australian who beat two Olympic champions to win the Diamond League 1,500m final in 3:30.14
text: Cameron Myers, the 20-year-old Australian who beat two Olympic champions to win the Diamond League At just 20, Australian middle-distance runner Cameron Myers has produced the biggest victory of his young career, winning the men's 1,500 metres at the 2026 Diamond League Final in Brussels. Myers clocked 3:30.14, edging Kenya's Phanuel Kipkosgei Koech by just 0.04 seconds in a dramatic finish. According to Reuters and Adelaide Now, Myers overcame a field packed with some of the world's leading middle-distance runners, including the two most recent Olympic champions in the event, American Cole Hocker and Norway's Jakob Ingebrigtsen. Hocker finished seventh in 3:30.80, while Ingebrigtsen placed fourth in 3:30.52. The victory made Myers only the eighth Australian to win a Diamond League Final and capped a breakthrough season in which he has established himself as one of the country's most promising middle-distance athletes. A dramatic finish in Brussels The men's 1,500m final brought together a remarkably strong field, with Olympic champions, international medal contenders and several of the world's fastest runners lining up in Brussels. Myers entered the race as one of Australia's rising stars, but the quality of the field presented an enormous challenge. The race remained tightly contested through the final stages. Myers positioned himself within striking distance before making his decisive move in the home straight. That strategy paid off. Myers produced a powerful finishing kick to overtake the runners around him and narrowly beat Koech to the line. Myers finished in 3:30.14, Koech in 3:30.18 and American Ethan Strand in 3:30.50. Ingebrigtsen followed in fourth with 3:30.52, while Yared Nuguse, Hobbs Kessler and Hocker completed the next three places. The margin between first and second was only four hundredths of a second, highlighting just how close the race became in its final metres. Myers' rapid rise The Brussels victory did not come out of nowhere. Myers has been building an impressive rÃ©sumÃ© throughout 2026 and has steadily established himself among the world's elite 1,500m runners. One defining moment of his season came in June at the Paris Diamond League meeting, where he ran 3:28.00 to set an Australian national record. That performance also ranked among the fastest 1,500m times in the world this year. He later won the mile at the Prefontaine Classic in Eugene, recording 3:46.06. Myers also earned a silver medal in the mile at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, finishing behind Scottish world-record holder Josh Kerr. Just days before the Diamond League Final, he won the 1,500m at the ISTAF meeting in Berlin in 3:30.96. His consistency across different competitions has helped transform him from a promising young Australian runner into a serious international contender. Beating Olympic champions What made the Brussels victory particularly significant was the strength of the athletes Myers defeated. Ingebrigtsen won the Olympic 1,500m title at the Tokyo Games, while Hocker captured Olympic gold in the event at Paris 2024. Both were expected to be major contenders in Brussels, yet neither finished on the podium. Ingebrigtsen crossed the line fourth in 3:30.52, while Hocker finished seventh in 3:30.80. The result demonstrated that Myers could compete successfully against established champions rather than simply winning when the biggest names were absent. The Australian's victory also came in a race where the top seven runners all finished within less than a second of one another, making his ability to time his final acceleration particularly important. A new chapter for Australian athletics Myers' Diamond League triumph represents another important milestone for Australian middle-distance running. The official Diamond League profile now lists him as a Diamond League Final winner and records his personal best of 3:28.00 in the 1,500m. The 20-year-old's rise has been especially notable due to his rapid progression. His national record in Paris, international victories and Commonwealth Games medals have all come in a single breakthrough season. His Brussels victory now adds one of the sport's most prestigious annual titles to that record. More importantly, beating two Olympic champions in a tightly fought final suggests Myers is no longer simply viewed as Australia's next big middle-distance prospect. He has already shown that he can deliver when competing against the best in the world, and at only 20, he may have several more years to build on that breakthrough. title: Inspiring story of the day: âHaving a dad with a big name doesnât do the work for youâ - How Trinity Rodman rose above Dennis Rodmanâs shadow, lived in motels, and built her own soccer legacy
text: Inspiring story of the day: âHaving a dad with a big name doesnât do the work for youâ - How Trinity Rodman rose above Dennis Rodmanâs shadow, lived in motels, and built her own soccer legacy Trinity Rodman has built a soccer career that now stands on its own. The Washington Spirit star is a 2024 Olympic gold medalist, a 2021 NWSL champion and, as of January 2026, the highest-paid player in NWSL history. But her childhood looked very different from what many people expected from the daughter of NBA legend Dennis Rodman . Trinity and her brother DJ once lived with their mother, Michelle Moyer, in a Ford Expedition and cheap motels in Newport Beach. Through those difficult years, Michelle kept life feeling normal for her children. That bond helped shape Trinity into the player she is today. How did Trinity Rodman live in a car despite being Dennis Rodmanâs daughter Having a famous father did not mean Trinity Rodman grew up with an easy life. After Dennis Rodman and Michelle Moyer separated, Trinity, her brother DJ and their mother faced serious money problems. For a period, they moved between a Ford Expedition and motels when Michelle could afford a room. The situation was especially strange because they were living in Newport Beach, where Trinity went to a wealthy school. She has spoken about seeing classmates arrive in expensive cars while her own family was trying to work out where they would stay. On Call Her Daddy , Trinity explained just how unusual those years were: âWe had a Ford Expedition and we lived in that for a little bit. Mind you, in Newport Beachâ¦ So imagine living in a car going to a rich school when everybody else is in Rolls-Royces and Range Rovers. But my mom tried to make every situation seem smoother than it actually was. For me and DJ, it was never embarrassing because we had each other and we had our mom.â For Trinity and DJ, however, those memories were not only painful. Their mother tried hard to make sure they still had happy childhood moments. At motels, they could eat breakfast, use the pool and spend time together before school. That helped the children see their family life differently from how an outsider might have seen it. What did Trinity Rodman say about her relationship with Dennis Rodman Trinityâs relationship with Dennis Rodman has remained one of the most talked-about parts of her story, but it has also been one of the most painful. She has said that her father was often absent while she was growing up and that there were long periods when they had little contact. That distance became impossible to ignore as Trinity began making a name for herself in soccer. Instead of being known only as an athlete, she was repeatedly asked about being Dennis Rodmanâs daughter. She later spoke openly about how difficult that connection could feel: âHeâs a person. Heâs not a dad. Maybe by blood, but nothing elseâ¦ Hearing his voice is painful because itâs missing him mixed with the fact that heâs an alcoholic. I answer the phone now for my conscience, but it took me a long time to realize that having a dad with a big name doesnât do the work for you. I had to build everything myself.â Dennis has also publicly admitted that he was not the father he wanted to be. At his Basketball Hall of Fame induction, he said he wished he had been a better father. For Trinity, though, her own career could not depend on her fatherâs reputation. Her speed, finishing, attacking ability and work on the field became the things that made people remember her. Why does Trinity Rodman call Michelle Moyer her role model? If Dennis Rodman gave Trinity a famous last name, Michelle Moyer gave her the support that helped her grow into a professional athlete. Michelle raised Trinity and DJ largely as a single mother and remained closely involved in Trinityâs soccer journey. The Guardian reported in 2021 that Trinity saw her mother as her main support system. That feeling has remained central to how she talks about her childhood and her success. Trinity Rodman put it simply: âMy mom wasnât in the NBA, but sheâs my role model. She is my world, my rock, and my right hand. Sheâs the strongest person I know. People always say, âOh, you get your athleticism from your dad,â but my work ethic, my heart, my grit, and the woman I am today-thatâs 100% my mom.â That is an important part of Trinity Rodmanâs story because her biggest influence was not another famous athlete. It was the person who was there when money was tight, when the family had nowhere stable to stay and when Trinity was still only a young girl trying to understand her world. How did Trinity Rodman turn a difficult childhood into a soccer career Trinity Rodmanâs soccer career moved quickly once she reached the professional level. She entered the NWSL with the Washington Spirit in 2021 and became the youngest player ever selected in the leagueâs draft at the time. She went on to win the NWSL Rookie of the Year award and helped the Spirit win the league championship that same year. Her rise continued with the U.S. womenâs national team. She became an important attacking player for the USWNT and was part of the squad that won Olympic gold at the 2024 Paris Games. The success also changed the way her name was viewed. Instead of being introduced mainly as Dennis Rodmanâs daughter, Trinity became a major soccer star in her own right. In January 2026, she reached another major point in her career when she re-signed with the Washington Spirit on a deal worth more than $2 million per year. The agreement made her the highest-paid player in NWSL history. That achievement says a lot about how far she has come. The girl who once went to school after sleeping in a car is now one of the biggest names in American womenâs soccer. Why is Trinity Rodmanâs story inspiring beyond soccer Trinity Rodmanâs story is not simply about becoming famous despite having a difficult childhood. It is about how she chose to define herself. She could have spent her career being introduced through her fatherâs name. Instead, she has built an identity around her own performances and the people who stood beside her. Her mother remained a constant presence, while soccer gave Trinity a place where her effort could speak for itself. title: One Tech Tip: How to avoid Celine Dion ticket scams as she makes her grand concert comeback
text: Celine Dion Based on their experience of hosting Taylor Swift, the management team at the Paris venue for Celine Dion 's grand concert comeback is bracing to deliver devastating news to hundreds of her fans: 'Sorry, you appear to have been scammed, your tickets are fake. ' The Grammy-winning star's long-awaited return to the concert stage after years away from touring has unleashed massive pent-up demand for tickets. It's a perfect storm for scammers who have wormed their way into fans' online communities and set up fraudulent ticketing websites to manipulate and rob fans of both their money and hopes of being able to say, "I was there." "Where there is massive demand and widespread excitement, fraudsters see a golden opportunity," says Group-IB, a Singapore-based cybersecurity firm that works with the international police agency Interpol and others. The first of the 26 shows is Saturday. Here are some tips to avoid the traps: For the few tickets left, use only authorized sites The Plenitude Arena, hosting Dion for 16 dates in September and October and another 10 in May, says the highest risk of scams is when tickets first go on sale - which was April for the upcoming concerts and June for the 2027 series - and in the shows' immediate build-up. "That's when the public will be very exposed to these scammers," Celine Trioux, the arena's marketing director, said in an Associated Press interview. "People are going to wake up and think, 'Oh, right, I didn't get a ticket, everyone is going, I want to go,' or 'I've seen the first show all over social media, it looks amazing, I'm going to find a ticket by any means possible.' And that's also when the scammers will be out in force." The shows sold out immediately, although a few VIP packages with Champagne and other perks are still available for between 1,099 euros and 2,990 euros (US$1,276 and $3,473) on the arena's website. One other possibility is to buy tickets from people who no longer want theirs. But the only way to do that safely is on three sites that are authorized for resales: AXS France, Ticketmaster France and Fnac Spectacles, Trioux said. There are unlikely to be many of those. Generally, just 4% to 8% of people who buy tickets for the arena end up not wanting or not being able to use them. "I strongly advise against buying a ticket from an individual or from someone advertising it on social media, because there's no way to know whether it's genuine or whether the same ticket will also be sold to other people," Trioux said. Check URLs to avoid fraudulent sites Group-IB says it found an array of fraudulent websites that impersonated official ticketing platforms as well as the official sites for Dion and for the arena. Some URL web addresses were close to the real thing, like celinedion.co (instead of celinedion.com), ticketmaster-celinedion.fr (instead of ticketmaster.fr ) or axs-billetterie.com (instead of axs.com ). "The first reflex should always be to check the website's URL," Trioux said. She said lawyers identified nearly 200 fraudulent Dion-related sites and social media accounts that offered tickets but that "when we shut down one copycat website, another one opens." "It's a constant battle," Trioux added. "It's impossible to close them all because technology is advancing faster than legal authorities can act." The Paris concert section of Dion's site has clickable links to all of the authorized ticket sellers. The arena says it will help fraud victims Group-IB says fraudsters appear to have reused scamming tools that were also deployed to target Oasis fans when the Britpop band reunited for a tour in 2025 and during Swift's 2023-2024 Eras tour. When Swift played four Paris shows in 2024, the Plenitude Arena had to turn away about "400 to 500 people who had been duped," Trioux said. She said that for Dion, the arena is expecting possibly hundreds of fraud victims each night. The concert series is a major milestone for the 58-year-old Quebec-born singer, her first since she revealed in 2022 her diagnosis with stiff-person syndrome, a rare neurological disorder. She last performed briefly in Paris at the opening ceremony of the Olympic Games in 2024, wowing with "Hymne a l'amour" (Hymn to love) from atop the Eiffel Tower in the rain. Fans are traveling from far afield to reconnect with one of the most decorated artists in pop music history. For those who have been scammed, the shock could be brutal. "We'll have a complaints desk for all these people, because they will generally discover the problem at the entrance, when they present their fake ticket," Trioux said. "Staff will be there to receive them and explain the procedure to follow if they wish to file a police complaint." Get the latest technology news and updates. Download the TOI App.

However, sheâd talked about wanting kids for ages, even made it part of her 10-year plan back in a YouTube video from 2019. "I want to do more movies, I want to have babies," she said, sounding almost giddy at the thought. Who is Michael Polansky ? Meanwhile, Gagaâs relationship with Polansky has always stood out for how ordinary it feels, especially compared to Gagaâs public life, which is all about wild outfits, huge performances, and endless reinvention. Polansky, on the other hand, isnât famous. Heâs not a musician or actor. Actually, heâs a Harvard graduate whoâs spent his life in the world of tech, investments, and philanthropy. He keeps a pretty low profile, despite being connected to some huge names, like Sean Parker (from Napster) and the early Facebook president. Polansky runs the Parker Foundation and has poured energy into cancer research and civic projects. His day-to-day moves are often more boardroom than backstage. Lady Gaga and Michael Polansky: A look back at their relationship The two of them met at a charity event in 2019 (which, letâs be honest, fits the philanthropic streak they both share). Public sightings started popping up right around New Yearâs Eve. Then COVID hit, and the pair bunkered down, living out the lockdown as a couple navigating something totally new. Unlike a lot of couples who got pulled apart by the stress and isolation, it sounds like Gaga and Polansky only got closer. And heâs not just âthe guy Lady Gaga dates.â Heâs gotten to know Stefani Germanotta, the woman behind the glitter and persona. Polanskyâs spoken out about how losing privacy has been tough, but their home life is surprisingly normal. You can almost picture them making breakfast or wrangling their dogs in sweatpants, worlds away from stadium lights. After a few years, they got engaged in 2024. Gaga announced it at the Paris Olympics, calling Polansky her fiancÃ©. They donât want a giant wedding, probably no circus of celebrities, more like a small celebration with family and close friends. Polansky even said in an interview that they already felt married in most ways. Rumors swirled about a secret marriage, especially during Gagaâs low-profile stretches, but thereâs never been an official confirmation. So, for now, theyâre engaged. Why Polansky, if one asks? Gagaâs described him in interviews as warm, kind, and genuine. Heâs supportive and, importantly, they bond over giving back â not just dropping checks, but rolling up their sleeves for meaningful causes. Their partnership feels rooted in the everyday: sharing meals, talking about raising kids, and dreaming up what kind of parents theyâll be. Gagaâs always been honest: she craves motherhood, and Polansky couldnât wait to be a dad. Together, they agreed their children should have the freedom to build identities independent of their parentsâ fame. Interestingly, Polansky has stepped into Gagaâs creative world. He helped with music tied to her projects like "Harlequin" and "Mayhem." Tech guy meets pop star, which is an unexpected mix, but somehow it works. He supports her art, but stays out of the spotlight. Now, with their first child, Gagaâs wish comes true. She called parenthood her ânext starring roleâ and seems determined to protect their family from the chaos that comes with celebrity. Theyâre keeping the details private; itâs not just a move, itâs a statement. Thatâs really what sets their story apart. Gagaâs spent years living in the public eye, but her family life with Polansky unfolds quietly. Theirs is a love story grounded in philanthropy, surviving lockdown, getting engaged, planning for kids, and now becoming parents. Itâs not about grand gestures â itâs about everyday moments.

title: Neeraj Chopraâs injury battles: From elbow surgery in 2019 to an ankle ligament tear in 2026 - the setbacks and comebacks that defined his career
text: Neeraj Chopraâs injury battles Neeraj Chopraâs career has been defined by historic throws, Olympic medals and a relentless pursuit of excellence. But alongside those milestones has been a recurring challenge: injuries that have repeatedly interrupted his season. Neeraj Chopra has been ruled out of the 2026 Asian Games and the remainder of the season after suffering an ankle ligament tear during training. The injury comes just days after he finished second at the Lausanne Diamond League with a season-best 88.05m. It is another frustrating setback for the two-time Olympic medallist, who had only recently returned from a lengthy injury layoff. Here is a look at the major injury setbacks that have disrupted his career. 2026: An ankle tear ends his season Chopra's latest injury is an ankle ligament tear sustained during training. The injury rules him out of the Asian Games, the Diamond League Final and the World Athletics Ultimate Championships, bringing his 2026 campaign to an early end. It comes after a promising return to competition following almost nine months away from the sport. Neeraj Chopra (PTI Photo) 2025-26: A long road back from a back injury Chopra's previous major setback came with a back injury that kept him away from competition for around nine months. He had competed at the 2025 World Championships in Tokyo despite carrying the problem, finishing eighth. The injury subsequently forced him into an extended rehabilitation period. His comeback was delayed further in 2026, with Chopra missing the Doha Diamond League before eventually returning to competitive action. 2024: Adductor concerns before Paris The 2024 season brought another fitness scare. Chopra withdrew from the Ostrava Golden Spike after experiencing discomfort in his adductor. Chopra subsequently opted out of the Paris Diamond League, again because of his troublesome adductor/groin issue. He later explained that he did not want to take unnecessary risks with the Paris Olympics approaching. The decision paid off as Chopra stayed fit for the Olympics and successfully defended his place on the podium, winning silver in Paris. title: Who are Qinwen Zhengâs parents? Meet Zheng Jianping and Deng Fang, the people behind her tennis journey
text: Who are Qinwen Zhengâs parents? Meet Zheng Jianping and Deng Fang, the people behind her tennis journey Qinwen Zhengâs rise in tennis has been closely linked to the support of her parents, Zheng Jianping and Deng Fang. The Chinese star was born in Shiyan, Hubei, and started playing sports as a young child before tennis became her main focus. Her parents soon realized that she had the talent and drive to go further. From changing cities for better coaching to making major personal sacrifices, they played a big role in her journey. Who are Qinwen Zhengâs parents, Zheng Jianping and Deng Fang? Qinwenâs father, Zheng Jianping, had a sporting background of his own. He competed in track and field events in Hubei and was part of the provinceâs second-level track team during his high school years. After leaving sports, he moved into business and later ran an auto parts company in Shiyan that dealt with cars, steel and construction materials. His own experience in sports helped him understand the hard work needed to compete at a high level. When Qinwen was young, Jianping encouraged her to try different sports. A moment when she chose to run instead of taking a ride in the family car helped him notice how much she enjoyed physical activity. Tennis eventually became the sport she wanted to pursue. Qinwenâs mother, Deng Fang, came from a very different work background. She studied railway transport and worked at railway stations in Hubei, including jobs involving ticket sales. Her role later changed when Qinwenâs tennis career became more demanding. Deng left her job so she could spend more time with her daughter and take care of her during training and travel. The two parents supported Qinwen in different ways. Her father focused heavily on her tennis development and the decisions around her career, while her mother handled much of the daily care. Qinwen has spoken about how important both parents have been to her success. Qinwen Zhengâs tennis journey and how her parents supported her Qinwen was born on October 8, 2002, in Shiyan, Hubei. She began playing tennis locally when she was six, but her parents soon understood that she would need better coaching to develop properly. When she was eight, the family moved her to Wuhan, around 200 kilometers away, where she trained for several years. Her next move was to Beijing, where she received more advanced training. Then, at 17, Qinwen moved to Barcelona with her mother to continue her development and compete in Europe. By then, tennis had become a full-time commitment, and her family had built their lives around giving her the best chance to succeed. That path also came with a major financial cost. Qinwen has said her father made huge sacrifices to keep paying for her career, including selling the family home. Some reports have put the total amount spent on her development at around 20 million yuan, although that figure has not been independently confirmed. Dengâs sacrifice was just as important in a different way. After leaving her railway job, she stayed close to Qinwen and helped manage the everyday parts of her life, from meals and travel to making sure she had support away from the court. Qinwen has never hidden how much she values what her parents did for her. After winning Olympic gold in Paris in 2024, she credited them for helping her reach that level. Their approach was demanding, but it gave her the chance to build a career on her own terms. title: A 16-year interlude: Shannon Rowburyâs wait for Olympic justice & her medal
text: Shannon Rowbury KOLKATA: For Shannon Rowbury, the 2012 London Olympics never really ended. The US middle-distance runner finished sixth in the womenâs 1500m final that night, believing she had missed out on an Olympic medal. But what followed over the next 13 years was the unravelling of one of the most tainted races in Olympic history. Turkeyâs Asli Cakir Alptekin and Gamze Bulut, who finished first and second respectively, were later disqualified for doping. Russiaâs Tatyana Tomashova, who was initially fourth and subsequently promoted to silver, was also disqualified following a doping case in 2024. As a result, Rowbury was eventually elevated to third. In June 2025, IOC officially reallocated the medals, making Rowbury the 2012 Olympic 1500m bronze medallist. Now, 16 years after the London race, the American will finally receive the medal physically at Los Angeles Olympics in 2028 â in front of the people who matter most to her. âIâm an optimistic person, so I always try to find the silver linings,â Rowbury said in Bhubaneswar last month. âItâs been a very difficult thing. When I found out the news, my entire body started shaking. I started sobbing. It was so much of the frustration I had carried within me about the unfairness of sport.â The London 1500m final has since become infamous, with six of the top nine finishers either disqualified or linked to performance-enhancing drug use. For Rowbury, however, the story is no longer simply about what she lost in London. It is about what clean sport ultimately gave her back. âI try to have gratitude for the fact that I do get justice in my story,â she said. âI will now have the opportunity to receive my medal in front of my two children. They will see their mother being recognised for winning with integrity, winning the right way.â That sense of justice has also shaped what Rowbury does today. She works with US Anti-Doping and speaks at conferences and events, trying to bring a human dimension to the fight against doping. Asked about Indiaâs doping problem and what federations can do to bring down the numbers, Rowbury stressed that the answer cannot be limited to testing and punishment. âItâs not just about winning a race; itâs about sportsmanship and how you win,â she said, arguing for an ecosystem that encourages performance while making it clear that cheating carries consequences. âOnce there is a clear directive that if you are cheating and you are caught, that you will miss your eligibility or there will be penalties, then hopefully that will disincentivise that performance.â But Rowbury also believes the solution needs to begin much earlier, during the development of young athletes and the creation of strong foundations built around the right values. Her own experience has also changed the way she looks at athletes â and perhaps explains why her transition into broadcasting has felt so natural. Rowbury began broadcasting while she was still competing, covering smaller meets in 2017 before retiring from competition in 2021. She has since worked in various roles with USA Track & Field, World Athletics and several broadcasters, and won an Emmy for her work during the Paris Olympics. Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines For her, being an athlete first has given her a different perspective when she tells the stories of those still competing. That understanding has followed her to India, where she recently visited for the World Athletics Silver Level Continental Tour and worked on in-stadium commentary while also conducting a workshop for aspiring Indian broadcasters. But it is Los Angeles that now looms large in her mind. When Rowbury walks into an Olympic stadium in 2028, she will not be chasing another medal. Instead, she will finally receive the one she should have got 16 years ago. Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
