title: Trinity Rodman's US Open moment reveals an old habit in sports broadcasting: introducing women by their relationships first
text: Ben Shelton and Trinity Rodman. Image via: Getty Images Trinity Rodman was sitting in Ben Shelton's player box at the US Open on Tuesday when the cameras found her. The ESPN commentary that followed introduced her as âTrinity Rodman, also known as Ben Shelton's girlfriend, and also known as a member of the US women's national team.â The on-screen graphic was similarly arranged: âBen's girlfriend & USWNT player. â Rodman is, of course, Shelton's girlfriend. The two tennis and football stars made their relationship public in March 2025, after Rodman slid into Shelton's DMs. Shelton, 23, is one of American tennis's leading players, a left-handed power hitter who reached a career-high world No.5 in late 2025 and has already won four ATP titles in 2026, including the National Bank Open two weeks before the US Open. But Rodman has spent the better part of her career becoming recognisable without him. The 24-year-old is an Olympic gold medallist, an NWSL champion and the highest-paid women's footballer in the world. She is also the daughter of NBA Hall of Famer Dennis Rodman, another fact that has often followed her into introductions of her own. Soccer player Trinity Rodman celebrates after her boyfriend Ben Shelton, of the United States, won his match against Hubert Hurkacz, of Poland, during the second round of the U.S. Open tennis championships Wednesday, Sept. 2, 2026, in New York. (AP Photo/Kirsty Wigglesworth) The ESPN description prompted a familiar reaction from fans online, particularly because there was no shortage of things from Rodman's own career that could have been used instead. âGeezâ¦ she is so much more than Ben's girlfriend,â one fan wrote. Another put it more bluntly: âTrin is an Olympic gold medalist, NWSL player and then Ben's girlfriend. In that order.â Rodman's career does not need Shelton's name attached to it Rodman's football career began long before she became a fixture in Shelton's box. The Washington Spirit selected her No.2 overall in the 2021 NWSL Draft when she was 18, making her the youngest player ever selected at the time. She won the league's Rookie of the Year award and helped Washington win the NWSL Championship in her first season. Three years later, she produced one of the defining moments of her international career. In the 2024 Paris Olympics final, Rodman scored in extra time against Japan as the United States won women's football gold for the first time since 2012. She now has 13 goals in 57 appearances for the USWNT. At club level, her value has grown just as quickly. Rodman became the first player signed under the NWSL's High Impact Player rule and agreed a landmark deal with Washington worth more than $1 million per season through 2028, making her the highest-paid player in the league. FILE - Washington Spirit forward Trinity Rodman in action during the second half of an NWSL soccer match against the Portland Thorns FC, Friday, March 13, 2026, in Washington. (AP Photo/Terrance Williams,File) There is also the question of her surname, which has brought its own assumptions. Rodman has spoken openly about her complicated relationship with her father and rejected the idea that the name defines her. âHeâs not a dad. Maybe by blood, but nothing else,â she said on Call Her Daddy . âI love to have my last name and when I say Rodman, itâs not my dadâs name, itâs my name.â She has been less defensive about being known as Shelton's partner. In fact, Rodman has said she actually likes the term WAG , even while acknowledging why some people dislike it. âFor me, I think I like the term personally because, like I said before, I feel like 24/7 I'm on in front of cameras, and so I think I use the term WAG for me to simplify what I'm doing,â she said on Not Gonna Lie with Kylie Kelce in August. âFor me, saying WAG, it's me being like, âI'm Ben's girlfriend.â But I can understand why it's so hated.â She described being able to share that experience with Shelton as âthe best feeling in the worldâ, pointing to the fact that both are constantly training, competing and exhausting themselves doing the sports they love. That distinction matters. Rodman choosing to embrace the label is not the same thing as it being the most useful way to introduce her. This has happened before The US Open moment was not the first time Rodman's identity has been filtered through the people around her. At Wimbledon in 2025, she was introduced during one of Shelton's matches as âTiffanyâ and had her father mentioned in the same breath. This time, the mistake was different. Her name was right, her relationship was real and her football career was acknowledged. Yet the order still said something: Ben's girlfriend first, USWNT player second. Washington Spirit forward Trinity Rodman shoots as Seattle Reign FC midfielder Samantha Meza, right, looks on during the first half of an NWSL soccer match, Sunday, May 10, 2026, in Seattle. (AP Photo/Lindsey Wasson) There was plenty of room for a different introduction. Rodman was not simply another celebrity sitting in a tennis player's box. She was an Olympic champion watching another elite American athlete compete at one of the biggest sporting events in the world. Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines She can be Ben Shelton's girlfriend. She can be Dennis Rodman's daughter. She can even happily call herself a WAG. None of those things requires her own achievements to come second. At 24, Trinity Rodman has already built a career substantial enough to stand on its own. At the US Open, she happened to be there to support someone else. For once, she deserved the spotlight without needing to be introduced through him. Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

title: Paris Olympics displaced nearly 20,000 people: Local associations
text: NEW DELHI: Approximately 20,000 individuals were displaced from temporary settlements or shelters in the Paris area before the Olympics , according to a report released on Monday by a coalition comprising over 100 community organisations. "Le Revers de la MÃ©daille" (translated as "the other side of the medal") documented 19,526 people removed from informal dwellings between April 2023 and September 2024, describing it as authorities' "social cleansing". The report acknowledges potential duplicate counting of individuals who faced multiple evictions. The preparation for accommodating millions of Olympic spectators involved substantial infrastructure improvements, which allegedly included removing migrants and squatters from areas near event locations. Paul Alauzy, representing "Le Revers de la MÃ©daille", stated there was concrete evidence connecting these removals to Olympic preparations. "There are images, internal government documents, and eviction orders explicitly referencing the Olympics as justification," Alauzy said on Monday. The organisation's findings revealed 260 eviction operations from April 2023 to September 2024, showing a 41% increase compared to 2021-2022. Additionally, the displaced population included more than 4,500 children. French authorities have not yet commented on these figures. The city implemented stringent security protocols for the Games, particularly for the Seine River opening ceremony, requiring verification procedures and QR codes for attendance. In August, Ãle-de-France regional prefect Marc Guillaume stated during a radio broadcast that Olympic-related evictions had not increased, asserting that alternative accommodation was offered to all displaced persons. French President Emmanuel Macron discussed this matter in August, highlighting France's Olympic-related social achievements. "I'm not forgetting that we have succeeded in creating a social legacy for the Olympic Games, with more than 200 marginalised people who used to live on the streets around the venues now having a permanent home," Macron said at a conference on August 12, the day following the Olympics closing ceremony. The coalition's report suggests establishing a permanent Olympic venue and implementing sustainable practices to prevent future displacement issues.

title: Paris Olympics 2024: Your ultimate guide to the Summer Games
text: (Reuters Photo) The 33rd Summer Olympic Games are set to take place in Paris from July 26 to August 11, 2024, followed by the Paralympic Games from August 28 to September 8, 2024. Over 10,000 athletes will compete in 329 medal events. Hereâs everything you need to know about tickets, accommodations, transportation, and moreâ¦ Where to buy tickets for Paris Olympics 2024 ? Tickets for the Paris Olympic Games are available on the official website [tickets.paris2024.org] and the Paris 2024 tickets application. Approximately 10 million tickets are on sale for the Olympic Games and around 3.4 million for the Paralympic Games. For hospitality packages, visit [hospitalitytravelpackages.paris2024.org]. To ensure authenticity, it is advisable to purchase tickets only through these official platforms. Where is the Olympic Stadium? The largest stadium in France, Stade de France , located in the northern suburb of Saint-Denis, will transform into the Olympic Stadium this summer. It has hosted significant sporting events such as the Rugby World Cups and the World Athletics Championships over the past three decades. Best ways to get around Paris during the Summer Games Public transport is the most efficient way to navigate Paris during the Summer Games. The cityâs metro system consists of 16 lines serving over 300 stations. Travelers can purchase a rechargeable Navigo pass preloaded with journeys. The Navigo Pass is valid for trains, buses, and trams. Accommodation for Paris Olympics 2024 Itâs advisable to book accommodation well in advance. Options include Airbnb and hotel chains like ibis, Novotel, and Sofitel. The website [Paris je tâaime] offers a range of options, including hotels, youth hostels, and bed and breakfasts. New sports added to the Paris Olympics 2024 The Paris Olympics will introduce Breaking (Breakdancing) for the first time, with events scheduled for August 9 and 10. Additionally, Sport Climbing , Skateboarding, and Surfing will make their Olympic debut this year. A brief history of the Modern Olympics The modern Olympic Games can be traced back to April 6, 1896, reviving 1500 years after being banned by Roman Emperor Theodosius I. French educator and historian, Baron Pierre de Coubertin, played a crucial role in reestablishing the Olympics. The first modern Olympic Games were held in Athens in 1896, with 13 countries participating. As the world eagerly anticipates the Paris 2024 Olympics, these details will help ensure a memorable and seamless experience for all attendees.

title: Paris Olympics 2024: A comprehensive list of summer sports
text: The most awaited athletic event in the world, the 2024 Summer Olympics, finally kicked underway in Paris today. The event, which took place on a lively Friday night, presented Paris in all its beauty and set the stage for what looks to be an incredible Olympic Games. Renowned performer Celine Dion had a breath taking performance that stole the show at the celebration. The athletes broke with convention by skipping the traditional parade through the stadium. Rather, they opted to sail along the Seine River on exquisitely decorated boats that gracefully meandered through the lovely scenery of Paris. These athletes will compete in various sports on behalf of their countries. However, which sports were part of the original ancient Olympics? Which games are currently included in this yearâs Olympics and which arenât. Find here. The International Olympic Committee (IOC) organised the first ancient Summer Olympics, which took place in Athens, Greece, in 1896. The French nobleman Pierre de Coubertin established the committee, and the games were held from April 6â15, 1896. About 241 athletesâall of whom were menâfrom fourteen different countries competed in the game at that time. The competitors participated in 43 different games, which included boxing, sprinting, long jump, shot put, javelin, and equestrian competitions. The spirit of competition and the evolution of sports have since shaped the modern Olympics into the grand event we see in 2024. List of sports included in the Paris Olympics 2024 S.No. Name of the Sport 1 Archery 2 Athletics 3 Badminton 4 Basketball 3x3 5 Beach Volleyball 6 Boxing 7 Break dancing 8 Canoe Slalom 9 Canoe Sprint 10 BMX Cycling 11 Diving 12 Equestrian 13 Fencing 14 Football 15 Golf 16 Gymnastics 17 Handball 18 Hockey 19 Judo 20 Modern Pentathlon 21 Rowing 22 Rugby Sevens 23 Sailing 24 Shooting 25 Skateboarding 26 Sport Climbing 27 Surfing 28 Swimming 29 Table Tennis 30 Taekwondo 31 Tennis 32 Triathlon 33 Volleyball 34 Weightlifting 35 Wrestling Sports included in Olympics Archery There are five medal events in the current Olympic archery competition: mixed team recurve, which is making a comeback following its debut in Tokyo, men's individual, women's individual, men's team, and women's team. The archer is 70 metres away from the target in all cases. Athletics Along with cycling, fencing, gymnastics, and swimming, athletics is one of the five sports that have been competed in at every summer Olympic Games since 1896. Twelve men's track and field eventsâthe 100-, 400-, 800-, 1,500-, 110-meter hurdles, marathon, high jump, pole vault, long jump, triple leap, shot put and discus throwâhave been competed in at all the Games. Four women's eventsâthe 100-meter sprint, the 4 x 100-meter relay, the high jump, and the discus throwâhave been competed in at every Olympic Games. Badminton A Mixed Doubles event was added to the Olympic Games for the first time in 1996 in Atlanta. Badminton made its Olympic debut as a full-medal sport at the 1992 Olympic Games in Barcelona, Spain. Basketball 3x3 and 5x5 3x3 basketball, sometimes referred to as streetball or street basketball, is a casual basketball variant that is played all over the world. The 2010 Youth Olympic Games marked the sport's debut on the world scene. Four basketball gold medals will be awarded, with competitions for men and women to compete in 5x5 basketball and men and women to compete in 3x3 basketball. The Pierre Mauroy Stadium in Lille will host the 5x5 basketball games, while the Accor Arena (Paris-Bercy) in Paris will host the championship game. The Place de la Concorde, a sizable public square in Paris, will host the 3x3 games. Beach Volleyball Beach volleyball became an official event in 1996. Although There are usually three stages to the beach volleyball competition at the Olympics: qualifying, knockout, and medal rounds. Teams are split up into groups for the preliminary stage, and each group competes in a round-robin manner. A best-of-three set format is used for beach volleyball matches, with the first two sets going to 21 points apiece and a possible third set going to 15 points. Each group's top teams move on to the knockout round. Boxing Since boxing debuted in 1904, every Summer Olympic Games has included the sport, with the exception of Stockholm in 1912 when it was outlawed by Swedish legislation. 2012 saw the debut of women's boxing at the London Games. While female boxing matches last four rounds of two minutes, male boxing matches last three rounds. Breakdancing Breakdancing is one of four sports (sport climbing, skateboarding, and surfing) that would be included in the Olympic Games schedule for 2024 in Paris. Breakdancing in Paris 2024 will feature head-to-head "battles" with 16 athletes in each gender. Canoe Slalom The slalom kayak cross for men and women is a brand-new competition in 2024.Paddling a decked canoe or kayak, competitors attempt to complete a course of hanging gates on river rapids in the shortest amount of time. Canoe Sprint Athletes race on flat waters in lanes, in canoes (1 or 2 paddlers) and Kayaks (1,2 or 4 paddles). BMX Cycling (Freestyle, racing, mountain bike, road and track) There are events for both men and women in the BMX cycling category of the Summer Olympics. Individual BMX racing events for men and women were introduced to the Beijing 2008 Olympic program. In 2020, BMX freestyle events were introduced to the Olympic Games for both men and women. Throughout a 60-second run, the competitors showcased their abilities and inventiveness by utilising ramps and other obstacles in a "park course" competition. Diving The Olympic diving program currently consists of multiple events: individual 3m springboard, 10m platform, and synchronised events (all for men and women). Competitors can make their own dives or select from a list of dives that have been evaluated based on difficulty. Approach, takeoff, elevation, movement execution, and entry into the water all result in points. Equestrian At the moment, there are three horse sports offered at the Olympics: eventing, dressage, and jumping. In 1900, show jumping was added to the Olympic Games. In 1912, three-day eventing and dressage were established. Fencing The foil, Ã©pÃ©e, and sabre are the three forms of weapons used in Olympic fencing today. There are twelve fencing competitions at the Olympics right now. For both men and women, there are six medal events. Football The first team sport to be added to the Olympics was football. It made its Olympic debut at the 1900 Paris Olympics. In 1996, a women's Olympic football competition was introduced to the schedule. The women's teams are not limited by age, however the men's teams can only have three over-age players, and they can only have under-23 players on their rosters. Golf Golf and rugby were the two sports chosen by the IOC in August 2009 as new additions to the program for 2016. The Olympic competition for 2024 in Paris will be the same as it was in previous editions. The competition is a 72-hole individual stroke play match. For any medal ties, a three-hole playoff is utilised. Gymnastics Gymnastics is a sport that has three distinct competitions in the Olympics. They are as follows: Athletes in âartistic gymnasticsâ compete in both solo and team events using various equipment and floor routines. Participants in ârhythmic gymnasticsâ execute choreographed routines using handheld equipment. Trampoline: This sport entails competitors performing acrobatic manoeuvres like somersaults and twists in mid air while jumping on a trampoline up to eight metres in the air. Points are given for flight duration, difficulty, and execution. Handball In 1936, handball made its debut at the Olympic Games in Berlin (see Field Handball 1936). Twelve teams, twelve men's and twelve women's, compete in two groups in a round robin format in Paris before moving on to knockout rounds. For men, this format hasn't changed since 2000, while for women, it hasn't changed since 2008. Hockey The sport of hockey was first presented at the London Olympic Games for men in 1908. It was eliminated from the Olympics following the 1924 Summer Olympics in Paris following the founding of the International Hockey Federation (FIH) in 1928. In 1980, the women's competition was added to the schedule. Twenty-four teams competed in the men's and women's event (twelve for each gender). Judo Men's judo was first introduced to the Olympic Games in Tokyo in 1964. In 1992, it was recognised as an official sport. There are fourteen body weight divisions with seven male and seven female classes. In addition, there is a mixed team competition with six athletes competing in three weight classes each gender. Modern Pantheon Since the Stockholm Games in 1912, modern pentathlon has been a part of the Olympic program. The current Olympic movement was started by the French baron Pierre de Coubertin, who invented the sport. It consists of five sports that were formerly performed over two days, but more recently, it has only been held on one day. The Modern Pentathlon will remain unchanged from its previous iteration (with modifications planned for 2028). Rowing One of the staple competitions in the Olympics is rowing. Since 1900, it has been a part of the Olympic program. The first women's competitions were held at the Montreal Games in 1976. Every race takes place on a 2000 m (1.24 km) course. There are a total 14 rowing events in the 2024 Olympics. Rugby sevens The faster-paced, more thrilling variation of rugby known as Rugby 7s is played at the Olympics, with competitions for men and women. In 2016, rugby was introduced to the Olympic schedule. There will be twenty-four teams competing for the medalsâtwelve for the men and women. The rugby sevens contests will begin two days ahead of the opening ceremony for the first time. Sailing Since the inaugural Olympic Games, sailing has been a featured sport (although it was referred to as yachting until 2000). The sailing program has been expanded to include a kiteboarding event for the 2024 Olympic Games in Paris. There is now only one 470 mixed event, as opposed to the men's and women's 470 classes. Sailing Events (Paris 2024) Men's Single-handed Dinghy - ILCA 7 Skiff event - 49erFX Windsurfing - IQFoil Kiteboarding - Formula Kite Women's Single-handed Dinghy - ILCA 6 Skiff event - 49erFX Windsurfing - IQFoil Kiteboarding - Formula Kite Both men and women Double-handed Dinghy - 470 Foiling Catamaran - Nacra 17 Shooting Shooting has only twice been excluded from the Olympic schedule: in 1928 and 1904. The Olympic Games included women's shooting competitions for the first time in 1984. The mixed team skeet competition has taken the place of the mixed team trap competition in 2020. Additionally, there are now 340 shooters competing instead of the previous number of 360. Skateboarding The International Olympic Committee (IOC) took a vote in 2009 over the inclusion of roller sports in the 2016 Olympic schedule. Skateboarding was a strong competitor, but rugby and golf were chosen instead. Roller sports were included on the list of eight sports for the Tokyo Olympics in 2020 in 2013. Skateboarding and inline speed skating were included in the 2015 shortlist; however, only events involving street and park skating were allowed. Sport Climbing Three disciplines comprise the Olympic climbing competition: bouldering, lead climbing, and speed climbing. A mixed speed, bouldering, and lead climbing competition was added for Tokyo 2020. The speed event was split off from the lead and bouldering events in Paris 2024, bringing the total number of medal events and competitors up to 68. Male and female competitors can compete for gold medals in the combined bouldering and lead event. Surfing Together with four other new sports, surfing was eventually added to the 2020 Tokyo Olympic Games schedule after years of fighting for inclusion. It will be back on schedule in 2024, but this time held in French Tahiti. Swimming There are 35 swimming events in the pool for the 2024 Games in Paris, including the 4 Ã 100m mixed medley relay and 17 events for men and women. The 10km open-water swimming marathon for men and women is the other swimming competition at the Olympics. Table Tennis Since 1988, table tennis has been a feature of the Summer Olympic Games. Both men's and women's singles and pairs competitions are held. Chinese competitors have dominated the table tennis medals throughout Olympic history. Five things happen. Men's and women's teams, mixed doubles, and men's and women's singles are all open to competitors. Taekwondo One of the two Asian martial arts that are part of the Olympic program is Taekwondo; the other is Judo. Since its debut as an official Olympic sport in the 2000 Games, taekwondo has been a part of the athletic schedule. Tennis In addition to the men's and women's singles and doubles competitions, there has been a mixed doubles event since London 2012. Tennis has five medal events: a mixed doubles competition in addition to men's and women's singles and doubles competitions. Roland-Garros will host the clay-court competition. Triathlon The first triathlon competition took place during the 2000 Summer Olympics in Sydney. While there are differences in the competition durations used in triathlons across the globe, the Olympic distances consist of a 1.5-kilometer swim, a 40-kilometre cycle, and a 10-kilometre run. Three triathlon competitions are held in the Olympics: a mixed relay competition (a new event in 2020), a competition for men and women. Every competition has just one race with no heats for all participants. Volleyball Beach volleyball and indoor volleyball are the two types of volleyball played at the Olympics. Since 1964, it has been a recognised sport at the Olympics. In 1996, beach volleyball made its formal debut. The winners are determined by adding together the best performances in each lift. There are ten categories instead of fourteen (two fewer for men and women) than there were in Tokyo. title: Paris Olympics 2024: Indiaâs Olympics uniforms create a buzz for the wrong reasons
text: PTI Photo Bigger isnât always betterâ the clichÃ© was proved right during the Olympics opening ceremony. In Paris, the worldâs fashion capital, it was Team Mongoliaâs Seine-sensational gold-embroidered ensemble that scored big. Haiti (super arty), Czechia (splattered trench coats) and Sri Lanka (white silk) wowed too even though the US (Ralph Lauren) and Italy (Emporio Armani) pulled out the big guns. As for India, letâs say if there was a medal for the best ceremonial uniform, we wouldnât even be close. Though Indiaâs ikat-inspired kurta-bundi and sarees were designed by no less than Tarun Tahiliani, many thought it was a missed opportunity to celebrate Indian craftsmanship. While itâs rare to see a polarized social media agree on something, this time the criticism was almost unanimous. âToday, the Indian fashion industry is talked about for its traditional yet modern clothing. This was an opportunity to make something unique and creative.,â says Delhi-based fashion designer Shilpi Gupta. This was also the first time a designer had been roped in to design the official ceremonial attire for Team India. Fashion commentator Shefalee Vasudev says the debate shouldnât be about print vs handwoven as Tasva, a collaboration between Tahiliani and Aditya Birla Group, was contracted to design the contingent uniforms. âTasva is into quality mill-made fabric. Itâs not a handloom brand. If someone had wanted a hand -loom imprint, the contract would have been given to those known for their handloom signature,â says Vasudev. But she adds that even within the mandate, the aesthetics did not come together. Responding to the comments, Ashish Mukul, brand head of Tasva, told TOI that the ceremonial attire for Team India was crafted with a sense of national pride and an aim to balance tradition with modernity. âOur intention is to create an attire that represents Indiaâs rich heritage and ensure our athletes feel comfortable and confident,â Mukul said, adding that the fabrics, including cotton and viscose crepe, were selected for their practical and aesthetic qualities. Nutritionist Nandita Iyer, who does not consider herself a fashion expert, says she was left dissatisfied as a connoisseur of Indian textiles, crafts and handlooms. âAny such global event is a stage for us to proudly show -case our heritage and history and doing it with viscose fabric and Ikat print tackily stitched as a border seems like hasty work,â says Iyer. However, others pointed out the challenges of creating uniforms that balance aesthetics, functionality, and cultural representation. In a post on Instagram, Susan Thomas, ex-director of NIFT Bengaluru, pointed out that viscose is used for uniforms as â Olympics is a performance-driven event that hinges on fitness.â Designer Rina Dhaka pointed out that there are budgets and briefs to fill. âWhen we do productions on this scale, digital is used over weaves to give consistency and quality,â says Dhaka. For her, badminton player PV Sindhuâs beautiful smile lifted the ensemble.

title: Paris Olympics 2024: Winning start crucial for India's chances
text: Image credit: Hockey India For a country starved of an Olympic medal in hockey for 41 years, the Indian menâs teamâs bronze-medal finish at Tokyo in the previous edition, has fuelled the hope of the return of the âgolden era.â But Tokyo was three years ago. A lot has changed in world hockey, and Harmanpreet Singh and his men will have an arduous task over the next two weeks, starting with the New Zealand challenge that awaits them on Saturday. Ranked seventh in the world, India are placed in Pool âBâ that includes defending champions Belgium, Australia, Argentina and Ireland. The first three matches â against the Black Sticks (July 27), Argentina (July 29) and Ireland (July 30) â will determine the fortunes of India as they face Belgium and favourites Australia thereafter. The opener is a bit of a tricky contest for India, considering they havenât faced the 1976 champions in recent times. Although, statistically, India have an edge over New Zealand, the fact that they knocked hosts India out of the World Cup last year will not be lost on the team. While Argentina are proven to be tough nuts to crack, Ireland wonât be easy meat either and the Pro League, in which they ran the Indians close before going down 0-1 and 0-4, is proof enough. With all preparatory boxes ticked, itâs showtime at at the Yves-du-Manoir Stadium.

title: Paris Olympics 2024: Can the jinx be broken this time?
text: Manu Bhaker (AP Photo) PUNE: When Manu Bhaker takes on the eight-woman field on Sunday, she will not just fight for a medal. The Haryana shooter will also look to break a jinx or two. With a score of 580, Manu, 22, became the first Indian woman pistol shooter to enter an Olympic final and third woman overall after Anjali Bhagwat (Sydney 2000) and Suma Shirur (Athens 2004) in the 10m air rifle category. She has also become the third air pistol shooter overall to enter the 10m final in three consecutive Olympics . However, in both cases, the previous two couldnât win medals and finished eighth. Jitu Rai, Indiaâs top shot in the Rio Olympics in 2016 had also made it to the 10m air pistol final. The armyman, who was in his top form, could not go beyond eighth place, while unfancied Vietnamese Hoang Xuan Vinh became his countryâs first-ever gold medallist. In Tokyo, Indiaâs best shooter Saurabh Chaudhary had raised Indiaâs hopes when he entered the eight-man final after topping the field with a score of 586. The jinx continued to dash Indiaâs hopes as Saurabh finished seventh, while another first-timer Javad Foroughi of Iran clinched gold. For Manu, there is good news and bad. Barring Chinaâs Jiang Ranxin, who had won bronze in the same event at Tokyo and 10m air pistol mixed event gold, her other six competitors have never won a medal at the Olympics. However, this could make the field even stronger as everybody would want to win their first medal. Manu had a nightmarish exit in Tokyo after she finished 12th after a pistol malfunction in the 10m air event and 15th in the 25m pistol event. For her the medal will not just be an achievement, but also a redemption of sorts.

title: Paris Olympics 2024: Lakshya Sen on song in opening romp
text: Lakshya Sen (IANS Photo) PARIS: It was one match in which Lakshya Sen would have been wishing he could settle the issue in just two games. The 22-year-old managed just that as he snatched four game points from Guatemalaâs veteran Kevin Cordon to open his Olympics campaign with a 21-8, 22-20 victory in a Group L match. So commanding was the performance by Sen that the longest rally of the match lasted just 31 seconds. Lakshya flirted with the lines and smashed into the net for a flurry of unforced errors that saw the 37-yearold Cordon, playing in his fifth Olympics, lead 20-16. After losing three chances to push the match into the decider, the four-time PanAm champion thought he had won the second game and even began celebrating. But a challenge by Lakshya led to an overrule that made it all square at 20-20. Cordon lost another challenge to stare at match point and soon it was all over as the Indian packed his bags after a 42-minute workout. Sen, who came out on Court 1 wearing a white tee and blue shorts, hit cruise mode early in the first game as Cordon failed to match Senâs deception, power and precision. The first game was over in 14 minutes after Sen, who had Indian badminton legends Prakash Padukone and Vimal Kumar on courtside, opened with a deceptive shot. He soon ran away to a 6-1 lead before changing ends at 11-2. Sen continued his dominance and Cordon found the going tough as the Indian repeatedly attacked his serve. The first game was over in 14 minutes but it was a slightly different story in the second game. Realizing that his opponent was not a tough contender, Lakshya went for the lines and tried to smash his way ahead. The ploy didnât work as he made a number of unforced errors, allowing Cordon to claw his way back into the match. Sen was trailing 6-11 at the break and Cordon pushed all the way to 20-16 before the Indian decided to turn it on. It looked as Sen was making his rival run around the court and towards the end, Cordon was clutching his arm in pain after a few powerful smashes. The average rally lasted only seven strokes and 10 seconds. âI was not getting my timing right in the second game,â Lakshya said. Coach Vimal Kumar also felt he experimented a bit more as it was his first match. âHe got a little nervous after hitting a few shots wide in the second game as he was playing with the draught. He was also trying different strokes as it was his first match,â Vimal told TOI. Next up for Sen on Monday is Julien Carragi of Belgium, who pushed World No. 3 Jonathan Christie, before losing in three games. Only the group winner will advance to the last 16. Breeze for Satwik-Chirag too With the French fans in full flow, singing and cheering their fans, third seeds Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty broke their hearts with a 21-17, 21-14 win against Lucas Corvee Ronan Labar in a Group C match. The match lasted 46 minutes. The top-2 from each group advance to the quarterfinals. âFor Satwik and Chirag too it was a tricky first match. With the home crowd rooting for the French pair it was not easy but they managed very well,â Vimal said.

title: Paris Olympics opening ceremony: All you need to know
text: (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) The opening ceremony for the Paris Olympics will break from tradition by taking place outside the main athletics stadium. Organizers have provided hints about their grand plans but have kept specific details under wraps. Based on public statements and press leaks over the past few months, here's what we know about the concept, artists, and music: "Games Wide Open", the motto of the organizers, is reflected in their decision to move the opening parade from the stadium to the heart of Paris. Approximately 6,000-7,000 athletes will travel along a six-kilometre (four-mile) section of the Seine river, starting from the Austerlitz bridge in the east and ending at the Eiffel Tower, aboard 85 barges and boats. The event is expected to draw up to 500,000 spectators, who will watch from specially constructed stands with ticket prices reaching 2,700 euros ($2,900), along the river banks for free, and from the balconies and apartments overlooking the route. "Organising a ceremony on the Seine is not easier than doing it in a stadium... but it has more punch," chief organiser Tony Estanguet told AFP earlier this month. The parade, due to its immense size and intricacy, has never been fully rehearsed before the event. Thomas Jolly, a 42-year-old acclaimed theatre director known for his successful rock-opera musical "Starmania", has taken charge of designing the show. Jolly has assembled a talented creative team, which includes Fanny Herrero, the writer of the popular French TV series "Call My Agent", along with renowned author Leila Slimani and distinguished historian Patrick Boucheron. The show has been divided into 12 distinct sections, featuring approximately 3,000 dancers, singers, and entertainers strategically positioned along both sides of the river, on bridges, and near iconic monuments. A tribute to Notre-Dame cathedral, currently undergoing restoration after the devastating fire in 2019, is certain to be included, potentially featuring dancers on the scaffolding. The ceremony will commence at 07:30pm (1730 GMT), with two-thirds of the event taking place during daylight hours, followed by duskâJolly hopes for one of Paris's breathtaking summer sunsetsâand will conclude with a light show. The musical selection will feature a blend of classical pieces, traditional 'chanson francaise', as well as rap and electronic music. Aya Nakamura, the Franco-Malian R&B sensation, is expected to take the stage, despite facing backlash from far-right political figures. Marine Le Pen, in particular, claimed that Nakamura's performance would bring shame to France, stating that her appearance would "humiliate" the nation. In other news, the iconic French electronic duo, Daft Punk, reportedly declined an invitation to perform at the event. Meanwhile, renowned French DJ David Guetta, known for his international tours, was surprisingly not included in the lineup, much to his displeasure. When asked about the overarching theme of his work last week, Jolly simply replied, "love." He emphasized that his creations would serve as a tribute to the rich tapestry of cultural, linguistic, religious, and sexual diversity found both within France and around the globe, despite the potential risk of offending conservative sensibilities. "I think the people who want to live together in this diversity, this otherness, are much more numerous, but we make less noise," he told AFP. The opening ceremony of the upcoming event is expected to take a different approach compared to the previous year's rugby World Cup, which was heavily criticized for its outdated and stereotypical portrayal of French culture, including "baguettes to berets and the Eiffel Tower." The organizers, led by Jolly, are cautious about placing too much emphasis on France's historical role in shaping democracy and universal human rights, despite the significant contributions of its Enlightenment thinkers and the impact of the 1789 Revolution. "We wanted to avoid our natural tendency to lecture people," Herrero told Le Monde newspaper recently. And don't expect a three-hour tribute to French greatness to rival the nationalistic pageantry seen at the Beijing Games in 2008. "The opening ceremony in Beijing in 2008 was exactly what we did not want to do," Boucheron told Le Monde. The future remains uncertain, as many details are still being kept secret. If Aya Nakamura were to take the stage, it would be a significant event, especially in the wake of recent parliamentary elections. The far-right, known for its anti-immigration stance, secured an unprecedented 143 seats in the national parliament. Jolly has strongly suggested that the waters of the Seine might play a role in the upcoming events, possibly featuring the emergence of a submersible or submarine. "You have the sky, you have bridges, you have water, you have banks, you have so much space to make poetry," Jolly told reporters last week. "So why not under the river also?" The most significant event of the entire occasion could be the conclusion, provided that all attendees return home unharmed. Since its announcement in 2021, the ceremony has caused French law enforcement to experience intense anxiety due to the challenges associated with ensuring the safety of such a large number of individuals across an extensive metropolitan region.

title: Celine Dion makes a rare appearance in Paris ahead of the 26th residency show, which marks her much-awaited musical return after 2022 Stiff-Person Syndrome diagnosis
text: Celine Dion makes a rare appearance ahead of her Paris residency from September to October. (Instagram) Celine Dion has been prepping hard for her Plenitude Arena residency in Nanterre, France. Since sharing her diagnosis of Stiff-Person Syndrome (SPS) in 2022, the beloved singer has chosen to stay away from the limelight, focusing on recovering and improving her health and her voice. Ahead of her big musical return, the singer was spotted on the streets of Paris. Celine Dion makes a rare appearance in two years ahead of her musical return Harperâs Bazaar reported that ahead of her upcoming residency show, Celine Dion landed in Paris in style. She made her first public appearance in almost two years as she headed out onto the streets. The singer was all smiles as she waved at all of the fans who had gathered around to catch a glimpse of her in front of the hotel that she was staying at, Le Royal Monceau - Raffles Paris. Watch Adele's Very Emotional Encounter With Celine Dion At Las Vegas Concert The âMy Heart Will Go Onâ singer wore a beige-colored double-breasted trench coat. Along with this, she opted to wear a simple black top, as well as a pair of stunning black boots and oversized sunglasses. More about Celine Dionâs residency Celine Dion will headline a 26-show residency at the Plenitude Arena in Nanterre, France. The residency, which was earlier announced in March this year, was originally supposed to be for only 16 shows. However, reports at the time revealed that more than 9 million people worldwide had signed up for the early access passes for the residency. This prompted the singer and the organisers to extend it by ten more days. The set is supposed to run from September to October; however, extra shows have been added to new 2027 dates due to the high demand. The additional dates have been added for May 2027. What is Stiff-Person Syndrome (SPS)? According to Cleveland Clinic, âStiff person syndrome is a rare, chronic condition that causes muscle stiffness and painful muscle spasms. The severity of symptoms varies from person to person. Thereâs no cure for stiff person syndrome, but treatment can help manage symptoms and slow the progression of the condition.â Following the singerâs announcement that she has been diagnosed with SRS, her doctors encouraged her to rest and stop touring to recover. The singer had to cancel the remainder of her âCourage World Tour.â Dionâs last performance was in 2024 for the opening ceremony of the Paris Olympics. title: Athletes' village handed over to Paris Olympics organisers
text: (Reuters photo) PARIS: The organisers of the Paris Olympics took possession of the newly built athletes' village on Thursday on schedule, reinforcing growing confidence that they will be ready for the Games. At an inauguration ceremony in northern Paris, chief organiser Tony Estanguet received a symbolic key for the complex in front of VIPs including President Emmanuel Macron. "It's a demonstration that we have honoured our commitments," Macron told reporters, who told workers they should be "proud" of delivering the village "on time and in budget." Organisers will spend the next four months fitting out the village with more than 300,000 items of furniture and decoration ahead of the first arrivals by athletes from July 18. The site comprises around 40 different low-rise tower blocks and will include a 24-hour restaurant, an alcohol-free bar and leisure area, as well as training facilities. The French state has contributed 646 million euros ($700 million) in public money, with the remainder from France's biggest real estate companies which have developed different areas of the 52-hectare site. After the Olympics and Paralympics, a third of the 2,800 apartments will be sold off to private homeowners, a third will be used for public housing, and the rest will be for rent including for students. Each building is different, with stark differences in facade design and colour. "We wanted architectural diversity which is a feature of European towns," Nicolas Ferrand, head of the games infrastructure group Solideo, told Macron. Seine-Saint-Denis is the poorest and most crime-ridden area of mainland France and is the focus of public investment for the Games. title: Paris Olympics preparations move up a gear
text: (Reuters photo) NEW DELHI: As preparations intensify for the Paris Olympics , security teams are thoroughly inspecting the Seine's banks in anticipation of Friday's unique opening ceremony. A rehearsal has taken place in secret along the six-kilometer route that will see 6,000-7,000 athletes sail on nearly 100 barges, witnessed by 300,000 spectators. Top International Olympic Committee (IOC) officials are also in Paris to prep for upcoming events. Police with sniffer dogs are ensuring the safety of the parade route. French police are joined by security personnel from Spain, Britain, and Qatar. The waterborne parade marks a historic first for an Olympic opening ceremony to take place outside a stadium. This spectacle has significantly impacted local residents, who need a special QR code to cross the Seine during preparations. Businesses, particularly in central Paris, report disruptions. Behi Samadian, 69, who owns a boutique in Saint-Germain-des-Pres, expressed concern about the decline in customers. "We've had far fewer customers than usual for the last two weeks. There aren't many tourists and lots of Parisians have left town. All our local clientele has gone," said Behi Samadian, 69, in a boutique in Saint-Germain-des-Pres. Team delegations have started to check into the athletes' village but some arrivals were delayed by Friday's global IT crash. "Like a lot of organisations, we suffered this global Microsoft outage," the Games chief organiser Tony Estanguet told reporters on Friday. "All of our servers were affected this morning." On a positive note, ticketing systems remained unaffected. Organizers report that 8.7 million tickets have already been sold, surpassing the 1996 Atlanta Olympics record, with sales ongoing for some of the 45 sports. High-profile athletes like American sprinter Noah Lyles are set for final pre-Olympics competitions at the Diamond League meeting in London on Saturday. Meanwhile, IOC President Thomas Bach and top officials are convening in Paris to prepare for a larger IOC Session later this week. Discussions will include the 2030 Winter Olympics' allocation, which is at risk of delay due to a funding disagreement with the French government. Russia will be notably absent from the Paris Games, contributing just 15 Russians and 16 Belarusians to compete, as many sports organizations have barred Russian athletes following the invasion of Ukraine. Those allowed must adhere to strict neutrality criteria. However, Global Rights Compliance, a Hague-based human rights foundation, asserts that two-thirds of the selected Russians expressed support for the invasion or have military ties. The IOC commented on this issue, stating, "it would not comment on individual cases."

title: American great Katie Ledecky wins Olympic 1500m freestyle gold
text: NEW DELHI: Katie Ledecky showcased her exceptional swimming prowess by securing a commanding win in the women's 1500m freestyle event on Wednesday, successfully defending her Olympic title and adding an eighth gold medal to her impressive collection. The American swimming sensation was in a league of her own, finishing the race in 15mins 30.02secs, setting a new Olympic record and finishing more than 10 seconds ahead of Anastasiia Kirpichnikova from France, who claimed the silver medal. Isabel Gose of Germany secured the bronze. Ledecky started the race with a strong pace, establishing a lead of a body length after the first 100m. By the halfway point, she had extended her advantage to five seconds. She maintained her relentless pace throughout the race, continuously increasing her lead and solidifying her status as the most outstanding distance swimmer in the history of the sport. The outcome of the race was never in question, as the 27-year-old athlete holds the last six world records and currently possesses the 20 fastest times ever recorded in the event. This victory marks Ledecky's eighth Olympic gold medal and her 12th medal overall, having also won a bronze in the 400m freestyle event, where Australian swimmer Ariarne Titmus emerged victorious. Ledecky is set to compete in the 800m freestyle event in Paris, where she will face a challenge from Titmus as she aims to secure a fourth consecutive title in the event.

title: Paris Olympics 2024: Why France's racially diverse society has united to boo Argentina
text: (Photo by Alex Pantling/Getty Images) PARIS: Thereâs an intriguing geopolitical tussle playing out here, threatening to blow up into an embarrassing diplomatic row. And football, racism and societal change are at the heart of it. On the eve of the Olympics , Argentina are discovering that they will not be winning any friendship prizes here this fortnight. Itâs ironic since locals here have been implored to shed their famous snootiness and inculcate an idea of âaccueuillantâ, or being welcoming for the Games. Argentina, in fact, will find it impossible to find any friends in the French capital, or any of the cities where Javier Mascheranoâs team is playing the football competition. On Thursday, at the Stade de France , Argentinaâs Rugby 7s team â the Pumas â was roundly booed during the national anthem. It left Pumas captain Gaston Revol surprised. âI wasnât ready or prepared for that reception,â Revol revealed. The crowd at the Stade de France was venting their ire at the Pumas, but it was essentially directed at the Albiceleste â the team of Messi, Angel di Maria and one Enzo Fernandez, current world champions after beating Mbappe and France a year and half ago. As of a fortnight ago, Argentina were Copa America champions too. After the Copa America triumph, Fernandez â Chelseaâs 55-million euro star â sang a song on the bus with racist overtones, mocking the composition of Les Bleus, the French national team, for its predominantly African-origin players, as being âfrom Angola,â or having a âNigerian motherâ or âa Cameroonian fatherâ. Playing his football in multi-ethnic Europe, working in a city as diverse as London, the tonedeafness displayed by the 23-yearold was baffling. Fernandez has since apologized but the French â with an estimated three million blacks or nearly 5% of the countryâs population â are not letting it pass. The episode has turned into a diplomatic row. Javier Milei, Argentinaâs populist right of centre president, is attending Fridayâs Paris opening ceremony and meeting president Macron to clear the air on the issue. Many are seeing this outrage within the prism of the difference in entitlement, perspectives and historical rivalries of the global north and south. It has not helped that Mileiâs deputy, vice-president Victoria Villarruel, came out in support of Fernandez, pointing to Franceâs colonial history. In the aftermath of the video, older videos emerged showing the French team mocking Messi after winning the 2018 World Cup. In another video, marquee French footballers Antoine Griezmann â a self-confessed Uruguayan by spirit â and Ousmane Dembele, of Mauritanian-Senegalese and Malian descent, were seen mocking the Japanese language as âching chongâ during a 2019 Barcelona pre-season tour. The duo apologized. The issue found a swift burial online. Maybe Villarruel was right in bringing up these double standards when she said, âWe never had colonies or second-class citizens. We never imposed our way of life on anyone.â But ask any Frenchman in Paris today and he will nod in approval at his countryâs new-found fervour. Once notoriously indifferent towards any attack on their complex social fabric, regular Frenchmen are now speaking out â in one voice. There is a sense of euphoria â and hope â in France. Last monthâs election results emphatically rejected the extreme right-wing ideology of Marine Le Pen, leader of the National Rally party and daughter of the French right-wing provocateur, Jean-Marie. But France opted instead for what many hope will be a more inclusive society, one that is largely free of Islamophobia and is not hostile to immigrants. âA left or right-wing government will not really improve my lot. Perhaps the right even have better ideas, but I voted for the left because Le Penn had a programme to exclude us immigrants,â 24-yearold Thomas Mehdi Labrar, a third generation French of Moroccan descent, said. France is brimming with African diaspora â Les Bleus is an active symbol of that, and Kylian Mbappe its shining icon. In fact, Mbappe, himself of mixed Cameroonian ethnicity, and other African-origin players often used the European football championship in Germany to remind people back home to vote and defeat extremists. Many said Franceâs indifferent form throughout the tournament and their limp ouster at the hands of eventual winners Spain was because their minds were occupied with the elections and the outcome. Statistics show that north African immigrants make up nearly 10% of Franceâs population â in Qatar in 2022, the nation was divided down the middle in whether to support France or Morocco in the WC semis. An estimated 1.15 million immigrants from Morocco and Tunisia make up Franceâs population â the largest ethnic group. This collective outrage following Fernandezâs chants is a manifestation of a growing sense of solidarity and unity in a multiethnic society that has come together to reject the far right. Till it lasts, Argentina can seek solace in the idea that their being booed is giving a complex society hope.

title: Paris Olympics 2024: All eyes on Manu Bhaker as shooters take aim
text: Manu Bhaker (AP Photo) PARIS: When shooter Abhinav Bindra broke Indiaâs 28-year-old gold jinx in the Olympics in 2008, it became a moment to savour for every sports fan in the country. It was followed up by two more medals in London, but since then Indian shooters have drawn a blank. The disappointment of Rio and Tokyo has kept haunting us and if India are to come close to their tally of seven medals in the last Olympics, the shooters have to start firing on all cylinders in Paris. Itâs a 21-strong shooting contingent competing in all 15 events and all eyes will be on pistol queen Manu Bhaker at the Chateauroux Shooting Centre near the French capital. She is taking part in three events â womenâs 10m air pistol, womenâs 25m pistol and 10m air pistol mixed team. Her failure in Tokyo keeps cropping up but coach Jaspal Rana doesnât want to pay too much attention to it, as she prepares to take the range for her qualification event in the 10m air pistol on Saturday. âTokyo is history. Manu is ready for anything and she is full of positive energy. Everything is in the hands of someone up there,â Rana told TOI here on Friday. If the 22-year-old makes the final, that will be on Sunday. For the opening day, experts feel there is every chance that India will start with a bang in the 10m air rifle mixed team event. India will have two entries in Sandeep Singh and Elavenil Valarivan and Arjun Babuta and Ramita Jindal. âExcept for Manu, every Indian shooter starts as an underdog. And that means less pressure, which is in contrast to what it used to be when the Bindras, Narangs and Sodhis started as favourites,â former world champion Ronjan Sodhi told TOI. Of the 21 Indian shooters, only four â Manu, Elavenil, Aishwary Pratap Singh Tomar and Anjum Moudgil â have competed in Olympics before while the rest of the contingent will be making their debut in the high-pressure, high-expectation event. That could also be a blessing in disguise as they are getting into the range without the burden of expectations. Whatâs also working in Indiaâs favour is the overflow of shooting talent in the country. Seven shooters, including world champion rifle shooter Rudrankksh Patil and trap shooter Bhowneesh Mendiratta, who bagged the quota places, lost out in the trials and their places went to seven in-form shooters. While Manu will be the centre of attention, thereâs hope around Asian Games champion Sift Kaur Samra (womenâs 50m rifle 3 position) and teen pistol shooter Esha Singh, who won four medals at Hangzhou Asian Games. Among the men, pistol shooters Sarabjot Singh and Arjun Cheema are both capable of challenging the best in the business. Also watch out for the Indian team in the mixed skeet event comprising Anantjeet Singh Naruka and Maheswari Chauhan. Gagan Narang, Indiaâs chef de mission and a bronze medal winner in 10m air rifle category in 2012, summed up the mood. âThings have changed since our times. These days the athletes come to the Olympics with the belief that they can win gold medals, participation isnât the only aim,â Narang said. Itâs on the current crop to ensure that by the time the shooting events wind up on August 5, the former greatâs words donât ring hollow. title: Paris Olympics 2024: Manu Bhaker qualifies for final of womenâs 10m air pistol to raise India's medal hopes
text: Manu Bhaker (AP Photo) CHATEAUROUX: It was a mad scramble on Saturday morning. Having returned way past midnight from the opening ceremony, it was a challenge to catch the 5.30 am train to this small, sleepy town 300km south of Paris. After a two-hour ride, a cup of espresso outside the railway station helped clear the mind. Another halfan-hour bus ride later, we reached the shooting ranges, set up in the middle of nowhere. It felt good to get the first feel of the action of Paris 2024 â the 10m air rifle mixed team event. The qualifications had begun, the hall was extremely crowded and a quick look at the scores gave hope. Of the two pairs competing for India in the qualification round â Sandeep Singh/Elavenil Valarivan and Arjun Babuta/Ramita Jindal â the second pair was at No. 5 spot, just 0.5 points behind the fourth team. There were just three shots each left to go. In the mixed events, only the top four qualify for the medals round â the top two fight for gold and silver while third and fourth battle for bronze. When it got over, Arjun and Ramita had missed the medal round by just 0.9 point â 628.7 to 629.6. Both actually had a good series of 10+ shots, many over 10.5 but that is what fine margins are all about. Sandeep and Elavenil too, did not shoot poorly (626.3) but could finish only 12th in a field of 28. However, the good news came in the afternoon. Manu Bhaker kept her hot form going as she qualified for the final of the womenâs 10m air pistol, finishing a creditable third in the qualifiers and raising hopes of getting India its first medal here. A little later in the mixed zone, Arjun and Ramita looked back at how close it was. âWe shot well. Did all we could have done on the day. It went as we had visualized it, the way we had planned it,â Arjun said. âI felt great about my shooting but got a bit disheartened by the fine margin. There was no lack of effort,â Arjun said, smiling through his disappointment. Asked whether their team had started a bit slow â each player gets 30 shots in 30 minutes â Ramita said it was strategy. âWe take time in the beginning to settle down and shoot faster towards the end. 15 shots in 10 minutes isnât difficult for us. The idea is to stay in the moment. We felt comfortable out there,â she said. Arjun, when asked if the competition felt different as this is the biggest stage, said: âI donât see any difference. It is the same lane, the same zone, the same target. Sandeep started with a scorching 10.8 but failed to stay at that level. It was good but failed to get enough high shots,â he said. Elavenil was see taking a small break to speak with her coach Suma Shirur after her 15th shot. Asked about it, she explained: âI wanted to have a little talk. I was seeking her opinion. It helped me relax and refocus.â Was she feeling the pressure? âThis is my life. This is what I do. I shoot for hours. I gave my 100 per cent. There is no turning back. It is something like meditation for me.â Later in the afternoon, in the menâs 10m air pistol qualification, Sarabjot Singh finished ninth and Arjun Singh Cheema 12th.

title: From Anaya Bangarâs cricket return to Imane Khelifâs Olympic gold controversy: The biggest transgender and gender-eligibility debates in sport
text: The biggest transgender and gender-eligibility debates in sport (Agency Images) NEW DELHI: Anaya Bangar's return to cricket has opened a much bigger conversation about transgender athletes in sport, one that now extends far beyond the cricket field. The former Mumbai Under-19 cricketer has received clearance from Cricket Australia to play women's community cricket in the country, giving her a route back into competitive cricket after beginning her transition in 2022. Bangar can participate in Premier Cricket, which Cricket Australia classifies as community cricket, immediately. Her pathway to elite cricket from March 2027, however, comes with eligibility conditions, including a requirement to provide a blood test confirming that her serum testosterone remains below the prescribed threshold and that she continues to meet the governing body's policy requirements. Anaya Bangar returns to cricket The decision has already divided opinion. South Africa all-rounder Marizanne Kapp publicly criticised Cricket Australia's position, describing the decision as "absolutely ridiculous" and arguing against transgender women competing in women's cricket. Bangar's case is therefore not simply about one cricketer. The Olympics have taken a very different route Laurel Hubbard: the Olympic milestone Few athletes illustrate that change more clearly than New Zealand weightlifter Laurel Hubbard. Hubbard became the first openly transgender woman to compete at an Olympic Games when she took part in the women's super-heavyweight weightlifting competition at the Tokyo Olympics in 2021. She did not complete a successful lift in the competition and finished without a result. At the time, her participation was viewed as a landmark moment for transgender representation in elite sport. Five years later, the IOC has adopted a fundamentally different approach. From Los Angeles 2028, transgender women who do not satisfy the IOC's biological-sex eligibility requirements will not be eligible for the women's category at the Games. Lia Thomas and the battle that changed American college sport In the United States, swimmer Lia Thomas became one of the most prominent figures in the debate. Thomas competed for the University of Pennsylvania after transitioning and became the first openly transgender athlete to win an NCAA Division I individual title when she won the women's 500-yard freestyle in 2022. Her participation triggered intense debate over eligibility, fairness and the rules governing transgender athletes in collegiate sport. The issue has since moved well beyond one swimmer. In June 2026, the US Supreme Court ruled that laws in West Virginia and Idaho restricting transgender athletes from participating on female school and college teams did not violate Title IX. The court's decision cleared the way for states to maintain such restrictions based on biological sex. Emily Bridges and the battle over cycling Emily Bridges. (Twitter Photo) Cycling produced another highly visible case through British rider Emily Bridges. Bridges, who had previously competed in men's cycling, sought to compete in women's events after transitioning. Her eligibility became the subject of intense debate in 2022 when she was ruled ineligible for the women's event at the British National Omnium Championships. The wider issue eventually contributed to a significant change in international cycling policy. The Union Cycliste Internationale, cycling's world governing body, changed its rules in 2023 and prohibited transgender women who transitioned after male puberty from competing in women's events on its international calendar. The organisation said its decision was based on the available scientific evidence and the need to protect equal opportunities in the women's category. Imane Khelif: The boxing controversy that blurred the lines Imane Khelif (Image Via Getty) The transgender debate in sport is also frequently linked to another high-profile case, but Imane Khelif's story needs to be treated separately. Khelif is not a transgender athlete. The Algerian boxer was born and raised as a woman and competed in the women's 66kg category at the Paris 2024 Olympics, where she went on to win the gold medal. Yet her participation became one of the biggest controversies of the Games. The issue stemmed from a dispute between boxing's governing bodies. The International Boxing Association (IBA) said Khelif had failed its eligibility requirements at the 2023 World Championships and claimed that testing had found her ineligible to compete in the women's category. However, the IBA did not publicly release the underlying test results. The IOC, which was responsible for the boxing competition at Paris 2024, rejected the IBA's position and allowed Khelif to compete. Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines The WNBA  debate too The conversation has also reached women's basketball in the United States. Indiana Fever player Sophie Cunningham recently reignited the debate after speaking publicly about transgender participation in women's sport. Her comments generated both support and criticism, forcing the WNBA to address an issue that had largely remained outside the league's immediate competitive spotlight. WNBA commissioner Cathy Engelbert subsequently told teams that the league would continue discussing transgender participation, acknowledging the growing attention surrounding the issue. The situation is particularly interesting because there is currently no openly transgender player competing in the WNBA. title: Paris Olympics 2024: Schedule, opening ceremony, mascot, venues, new events, tickets
text: Paris Olympics 2024 NEW DELHI: The 2024 Paris Olympics , scheduled from July 26 to August 11, is set to captivate the world as the City of Light prepares to host this grand event. Paris will become the second city, following London, to host the Olympic Games three times, having previously hosted in 1900 and 1924. The opening ceremony on July 26 holds special significance, as it falls on the same day as the closing of the 1924 Paris Olympics , creating a remarkable historical connection. In a departure from tradition, the opening ceremony will feature a magnificent boat parade along the renowned Seine River, promising an awe-inspiring spectacle for all in attendance. The paris Olympics opening ceremony date is set to be a memorable occasion that blends history and innovation. With an impressive 10,672 athletes from 206 nations competing in 329 events across 32 sports, the 2024 Paris Olympics is poised to be the most spectacular and inclusive event in the post-pandemic era. The organisers have made a concerted effort to promote gender equality, ensuring that this edition of the Games will stand as a testament to diversity and unity. When is opening ceremony scheduled? The Olympics 2024 opening ceremony time in india is set to kick off on Friday, July 26, in the City of Light at 11 PM Indian Standard Time. In a departure from the norm, the event will not unfold within the confines of an Olympic stadium. Rather, the participating athletes will traverse the River Seine aboard a fleet of boats. Lining the banks of the river, bleachers will be erected to host a staggering 300,000 onlookers. The aquatic parade will reach its zenith at the picturesque Jardins du Trocadero, where the concluding components of the opening ceremony are slated to occur. Paris Olympics mascot : The Paris Olympics has unveiled its official mascot, "Freege," which is inspired by the iconic Phrygian hat. This distinctive headwear, famously worn by French revolutionaries, was chosen to embody the spirit of freedom and to personify the allegorical figures that represent the French Republic. In a remarkable twist, the Olympic medals for the Paris Games will incorporate a piece of history from the city itself. Chaumet, a prestigious French luxury jewellery maker, has been entrusted with the task of incorporating 18 grams of iron from the Eiffel Tower, the legendary landmark constructed for the 1889 World's Fair, into the silver, gold, and bronze medals. These one-of-a-kind medals will be presented to the victorious athletes at both the Olympics and Paralympics in Paris, adding a touch of Parisian heritage to their achievements. Paris Olympics new sport: Paris 2024 will introduce Breaking as a new sport, with separate events for men and women, where participants will compete in solo battles. Additionally, Canoe Slalom will feature a new discipline called Extreme Slalom, involving four athletes racing simultaneously down a course. Sailing will also see the introduction of two new categories: IQFoil (windsurfing) and formula kite. Furthermore, athletics, shooting, and sailing will each have a new mixed event: the 35km walking mixed relay, the Skeet mixed team event, and the mixed Dinghy, respectively. Paris Olympics 2024 Venues: The 2024 Summer Olympics in Paris will be spread across 35 venues in France, with the majority of events occurring within Paris and its surrounding areas. However, some competitions will take place in other French cities, including Marseille, Lyon, Chateauroux, and Bordeaux. The organizing committee has emphasized sustainability by focusing on utilizing existing facilities instead of constructing new ones. Iconic venues like the Stade de France will host athletics and rugby sevens, while the famous Stade Roland Garros will showcase tennis and boxing. The Paris La Defense Arena and the Paris Aquatic Centre will share the responsibility of hosting swimming events. Some competitions will even be held at renowned Parisian landmarks, such as beach volleyball beneath the Eiffel Tower and various sports at La Concorde. Fencing and taekwondo will be hosted at the Grand Palais, while the Marathon will commence at the Hotel de Ville. The Olympic Games will also reach far beyond the city of Paris, with football matches taking place in stadiums throughout the country, sailing competitions in Marseille, and surfing events in Tahiti, a French island situated over 15,000km from the French capital. Where to watch in India? In a ground breaking move, Indian viewers will have the opportunity to watch the Paris Olympics for free, thanks to Jio Cinema and Sports18 TV network's commitment to providing comprehensive coverage. The Olympics will feature an unprecedented India Feed, allowing fans to closely follow the nation's athletes and events. Additionally, 20 simultaneous feeds will be accessible, ensuring that no moment is missed. TimesofIndia.com will complement the coverage with in-depth reporting and live blogs. While the official Olympics schedule is available on the dedicated website, it's important to note that it may be subject to alterations. Factors such as events exceeding their allotted time and unexpected situations can lead to changes in the schedule. Where to buy tickets for Paris Olympics 2024? For those interested in purchasing tickets, resold tickets are currently the only option available, and they can be bought through the official resale platform on the website. Mark your calendars for the paris Olympics opening ceremony date, as it promises to be an unforgettable event. With the Olympics 2024 opening ceremony time in india clearly set, viewers across the globe can prepare to witness this historic spectacle.

title: Who is Sam Kendricksâ wife Leanne Zimmer? Inside her Ole Miss track career and life beyond athletics
text: Who is Sam Kendricksâ wife Leanne Zimmer? Inside her Ole Miss track career and life beyond athletics Sam Kendricksâ return to the Olympic podium in Paris gave his career another major moment. The American pole vaulter won silver at the 2024 Paris Olympics after missing the Tokyo Games because of a positive COVID-19 test. It was his second Olympic medal after his bronze at Rio 2016. Behind that difficult stretch was his wife, Leanne Zimmer. The couple met during their time at the University of Mississippi and married in 2017. Leanne also had her own career in college athletics before moving into higher education. Here is what is known about Sam Kendricksâ wife. Who is Leanne Zimmer, Sam Kendricksâ wife? Leanne Zimmer was born on October 16, 1995, and grew up in Georgia. She attended the University of Mississippi, also known as Ole Miss, where she competed in track and field. Her main event was the 800 meters, but she also competed in cross country and other track events. Ole Miss Athletics lists her personal best in the 800 meters as 2:11.97, set at the 2015 Tyson Invitational. She was also part of the schoolâs distance medley relay team. During her college career, she earned SEC Academic Honor Roll recognition. Her time at Ole Miss was not always easy. An injury ended part of her indoor season in 2014, leading to a medical redshirt. Still, she returned to competition and continued running for the university. Zimmer studied anthropology at Ole Miss and later completed a masterâs degree in higher education administration. Her academic path eventually took her toward student support and advising rather than professional athletics. Public reports have described her work at Ole Miss as including roles such as Coordinator of First Year Experience and Academic Mentor. However, there is limited reliable public information about her current professional role in 2026, so claims about a specific present-day job should be treated carefully. How did Sam Kendricks meet Leanne Zimmer? Sam Kendricks and Leanne Zimmer met while they were students and athletes at Ole Miss. Kendricks was building his reputation as one of the universityâs top pole vaulters, while Zimmer was competing in middle-distance races. Their shared experience as college athletes gave them plenty of common ground. Both understood the demands of training, competition and balancing sport with studies. Kendricks won NCAA outdoor pole vault titles in 2013 and 2014 before turning professional. The couple married on December 29, 2017, in Oxford, Mississippi. Public reports also say they have a son, born in 2022. The family has generally kept details about their private life away from the spotlight. He tested positive for COVID-19 before the Tokyo Games in 2021 and had to withdraw. The Washington Post reported that Kendricks remained unhappy about how the situation was handled and later questioned whether he would return for the Paris Olympics. He did return. At the 2024 Paris Games, Kendricks cleared 5.95 meters to win silver behind Swedenâs Armand âMondoâ Duplantis. Team USA lists him as a two-time Olympic medalist with one silver and one bronze. As of 2026, Kendricks remains a two-time Olympic medalist, while Leanne Zimmerâs public profile is mainly tied to her Ole Miss athletic career, education and her family life with the Olympic pole vaulter. title: Jemele Hill slams âjealous of Caitlinâ narrative as Enes Kanter Freedom targets Indiana Fever
text: Jemele Hill slams âjealous of Caitlinâ narrative as Enes Kanter Freedom targets Indiana Fever Jemele Hill has challenged the growing media narrative around Caitlin Clark after the three-time WNBA All-Star made her senior national team debut against China at the FIBA Womenâs Basketball World Cup. Hill argued that repeated claims of players being jealous of Clark carry racial undertones that are often ignored. Her comments came after Linda Cohn questioned Aâja Wilsonâs decision to withdraw from the tournament despite Team USA citing health concerns. Meanwhile, former NBA player Enes Kanter Freedom has created another WNBA controversy by saying he wants the Indiana Fever to draft him in 2027 so he can play alongside Clark. Jemele Hill questions Linda Cohnâs comments about Aâja Wilson Hill addressed the issue in a Saturday thread, arguing that major media personalities can make strong claims about the WNBA without receiving enough pushback. She specifically pointed toward the repeated idea that other WNBA players are jealous of Caitlin Clark, saying the discussion has a racial element that deserves more attention. Hill wrote: âSo when people with big microphones start chiming in on the W and offering silly opinions, there isn't a lot of pushback or counter narratives. There's also the issue of race. This whole everybody is jealous of Caitlin Clark narrative has such obvious racial undertones. I promise you if the league were 70 percent white instead of Black, this would never be said.â Her comments followed criticism of former ESPN anchor Linda Cohn, who questioned why Aâja Wilson was not playing alongside Clark for Team USA. Wilson withdrew from the World Cup shortly before the tournament, with health concerns given as the reason for her absence. Cohn nevertheless wondered whether Wilson might have been uncomfortable with the attention surrounding Clark and questioned whether insecurity had influenced her decision. Cohn even imagined what Wilson could have been thinking, saying: âCould she be thinking, âI'm the four-time MVP, I'm the best player in the world. Why does everything have to be about Caitlin Clark?ââ Those comments quickly became a major talking point among WNBA fans and drew criticism from several prominent figures. Hill believes the focus on supposed jealousy takes attention away from what the players actually do on the court. For Hill, the bigger concern is that this type of speculation can deepen divisions among fans instead of encouraging meaningful discussion about basketball. She argued that WNBA players are elite competitors and deserve analysis based on their performances rather than assumptions about their personal feelings toward Clark. The debate comes as Clark begins another important chapter with Team USA. After missing the 2024 Paris Olympics, the Indiana Fever star finally made her senior national team debut at the World Cup, adding another major moment to her rapidly growing career. Enes Kanter Freedom wants Indiana Fever to draft him alongside Caitlin Clark While Hill was criticizing the conversation around Clark, former NBA player Enes Kanter Freedom created another unusual WNBA storyline. Freedom has publicly said he intends to enter the 2027 WNBA Draft, despite league sources reportedly making clear that he does not meet the eligibility requirements. His comments have been linked to his criticism of the league's transgender athlete policy.
